Playbite is a consumer-facing mobile gaming product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its company identity, public web properties, and domain security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: QiDZ Holding
providers.description: QiDZ Holding operates theQapp (formerly QiDZ), a consumer mobile platform that helps families discover, compare, and book activities, entertainment, and dining experiences across the United Arab Emirates and the wider Middle East (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh, Jeddah, Eastern Province, Manama, and Cairo). The app curates theme parks, water parks, indoor play areas, sports and creative classes, kid-friendly restaurants, camps, staycations, museums, and birthday and event packages, and offers a Q-Club membership with exclusive promo codes and discounts. Backed by 500 Global, QiDZ is a B2C mobile experience distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine specification, so this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: TOCA Football
providers.description: TOCA Football, Inc. is a technology-enabled soccer experience and entertainment company headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, founded on the training methodology of former US international and Premier League player Eddie Lewis. It operates two businesses: TOCA Soccer, a network of indoor soccer training centers across the United States, Canada and Mexico offering private training, classes, clinics, camps, youth and adult leagues, tournaments and pickup play; and TOCA Social, a soccer-themed dining and entertainment venue brand. Its training centers pair a proprietary ball-delivery machine and digitalized smart targets with the MyTOCA player app, which tracks session performance, player cards, leaderboards and progress. TOCA is the official soccer training partner of Major League Soccer. TOCA publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer program: its software ships only as end-user consumer apps and in-venue systems.

providers.name: Whip Media Group
providers.description: Whip Media is a SaaS company powering the global media and entertainment industry through its AI-native Helix platform, which connects content licensors and licensees across the rights-to-royalties value chain. Helix spans supply-chain modules for licensees (avails management, contract management, royalties processing) and distribution modules for licensors (asset order management, performance tracking, revenue recognition), plus AI-powered Title Management for metadata enrichment and standardization. Customers include NBCU, Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount, Sony, and Lionsgate. The company publishes an SEO llms.txt and reports SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II audits for a sixth consecutive year, but does not expose a public developer portal or documented API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IVP.

providers.name: Atari
providers.description: Atari is one of the founding brands of the interactive entertainment industry, originally established in 1972, and today operates as a global video game and consumer-hardware company. It publishes classic and modern titles, manufactures the Atari VCS console and retro hardware (Atari 2600+, Atari 400 Mini), licenses its catalog and brand, and sells games, collectibles, and merchandise through its official online store at atari.com. Atari does not publish a general-purpose public REST API; its developer surface is limited to Atari VCS content-submission guidance (developers email vcs@atari.com and use the VCS submission portal) and legacy HTML5 Atari Arcade SDK libraries on GitHub. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company — a nod to Mayfield's foundational 1970s venture investment in Atari — and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Z1
providers.description: Z1 is the API Evangelist network profile for the consumer social gaming app operated by Bunch Live, Inc., known publicly as Bunch and now rebranded as Mini Party (mini.party). The product lets friends hang out, play party games, and video chat together in real time on mobile, and connects with external services such as Discord. Bunch raised early venture funding (including a $3.8M round) and is tracked here as a 500 Global portfolio company. Bunch formerly operated a Bunch Developer Platform (the "Party Kit" voice/video SDK for iOS, Android, and Unity plus a Party Reservation API), but that developer program has been discontinued and the company currently publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal — this profile captures its identity, legal surface, and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Hidden Door
providers.description: Hidden Door is an interactive storytelling platform where roleplay meets fan fiction, letting players step into imaginative worlds and shape branching narratives through their choices. Players pick a pre-built world, add modifiers, create a character, and experience a unique story with a full cast of characters, where every playthrough differs. Creators can build playable worlds in as little as thirty minutes, then share, publish, and get paid when others play. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Homebrew and Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. Hidden Door ships a consumer web experience and publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. Sector: AI / entertainment.

providers.name: iQIYI
providers.description: iQIYI is one of China's largest online video streaming and entertainment platforms, delivering movies, TV dramas, variety shows, animation, documentaries, and original content across web, mobile (Android/iOS), and OTT/smart-TV devices. Beyond its consumer service, iQIYI runs a SaaS / OTT developer platform that lets partners launch their own branded streaming service with a RESTful API covering Video, Channel, Album, Search, and Player resources, plus AVOD/SVOD/TVOD monetization, analytics, audience management, and DRM. iQIYI also operates the QIYU XR developer platform for VR/AR device applications and maintains an active open-source GitHub organization. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of Hongshan and has been enriched from iQIYI's public developer surface.

providers.name: Start Playing
providers.description: StartPlaying (startplaying.games) is the largest online marketplace connecting tabletop roleplaying game (TTRPG) players with professional Game Masters for systems including Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, Starfinder, Warhammer, and many more. Players discover, book, and join online sessions filtered by system, platform, genre, playstyle, and GM reviews, while Game Masters build careers by hosting paid games across virtual tabletops. The platform also offers gift cards, learn-to-play one-shots for beginners, kids' games, and corporate team-building events. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a consumer web product with no public developer API.

providers.name: Zoog.A.I. Ltd.
providers.description: Zoog.A.I. Ltd. (Zoog) is a consumer application that lets families create personalized video books and songs for children. Parents and kids can read classic children's books, sing popular nursery rhymes, and turn them into personalized videos featuring their own family, then share those magical creations. Zoog is delivered as an iOS app (with an Android waitlist) and a companion website, and is backed by 500 Global. It has no public developer API surface, SDKs, or API documentation at this time; this profile captures its identity and web presence within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Playabl
providers.description: Playabl is a no-code, conversational game creation platform that lets anyone build games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Operated by Replkt, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator, Playabl turns natural-language prompts into playable games across genres including sports, idle, brainrot, dopamine, and think/puzzle categories, with no coding required. The product is a consumer-facing web application (playabl.ai); as of this profile Playabl does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Songtrust
providers.description: Songtrust is a New York City-based music publishing administration platform and a Downtown Music company. The service helps songwriters, producers, composers, and independent publishers register their compositions and collect global publishing royalties — including performance, mechanical, digital, micro-sync, and neighboring rights — through a network of 65+ collection societies and pay sources across 240 countries and territories. Songtrust's web-based dashboard provides song registration, catalog management, writer and publisher splits, royalty statement matching, metadata enrichment, weekly song monitoring, and quarterly payouts, while letting clients retain 100% ownership of their copyrights. The commercial model is a one-time $100 sign-up fee per songwriter plus 15% of collected performance royalties and 20% of non-performance royalties — positioned as a transparent flat-rate alternative to traditional publisher deals. As of this profile, Songtrust does not expose a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or partner integration portal; the platform is consumed exclusively through the Songtrust client dashboard at app.songtrust.com. Integrations and data exchange with PROs, mechanical rights societies, DSPs, and Downtown sister companies are operated internally rather than through a documented public surface.

providers.name: Zoog
providers.description: Zoog is a consumer mobile app platform that lets families create and share personalized video books and songs for children. Users read classic kids' stories or sing popular kids' songs while the app adds filters, effects, and music to produce custom animated videos that connect loved ones across distances. Founded in 2021 by Yoav Oren and Matan Guttman and backed by Techstars, Zoog is used by families worldwide. It is a consumer product with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: A24
providers.description: A24 is an American independent entertainment company founded in 2012 and headquartered in New York City that produces, finances, and distributes films and television, including award winners such as Everything Everywhere All at Once, Moonlight, and Hereditary. Beyond production, A24 runs a direct-to-consumer business spanning a merchandise shop, the AAA24 membership program, editorial "Notes," podcasts, and a mobile app. A24 is a portfolio company of Thrive Capital. A24 does not publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Autograph
providers.description: Autograph is a fan engagement and digital collectibles platform co-founded by Tom Brady and operated by LFG NFTs Corp. It recognizes and rewards fans by turning their passion for athletes, artists, and celebrities into access, experiences, and exclusive rewards. The platform consolidates fan communities and content into a single app, using web3 and NFT technology to let creators and public figures collaborate directly with their supporters. Autograph is a consumer product with no public developer API program at this time; api.autograph.io serves the app backend and docs.autograph.io is a private GitBook.

providers.name: Spacetime Studios
providers.description: Spacetime Studios is an Austin, Texas mobile game developer and the creator of the free-to-play "Legends" series of cross-platform MMORPGs, including Arcane Legends, Pocket Legends, Star Legends, and Dark Legends. Founded by veteran game developers, the studio operates a consumer-facing community forum, an in-game item web store, and player support channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its verified public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: Cameo
providers.description: Cameo is a consumer marketplace for personalized video messages from celebrities, athletes, musicians, comedians, and creators. Fans book a custom shout-out by sending a short script with personal details, and the talent records and delivers a bespoke video, typically within seven days, for occasions like birthdays, milestones, and celebrations. Cameo also runs Cameo for Business for branded talent content, sells gift cards, and offers a Red Carpet Rewards loyalty program. Cameo does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI; this profile tracks the company's public web, help, and security surface.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Take-Two Interactive Software API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: BuzzFeed
providers.description: BuzzFeed Inc. is a digital media company founded in 2006 and headquartered in New York City, best known for its viral entertainment, quizzes, pop-culture coverage, and commerce content. The company operates a portfolio of brands including the flagship BuzzFeed site, the news operation HuffPost, and the food brand Tasty, and produces video, podcasts, and shoppable content across web and social platforms. BuzzFeed is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: BZFD) and monetizes through advertising, brand partnerships, and commerce. It does not publish a general-purpose public developer API program; its public machine-readable surface consists of content syndication (RSS feeds), an advertising/partnerships business, and a security.txt vulnerability-disclosure program via HackerOne. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from an a16z portfolio lead and enriched with the provider's real public surface.

providers.name: Loftia
providers.description: Loftia is a cozy, solarpunk massively-multiplayer online (MMO) game developed by Qloud Games Pty Ltd, a remote-first indie studio founded in 2022 and headquartered in Sydney, Australia. Set across floating islands in a warm, sustainable world, players farm, craft, decorate, socialize, and build a life in the sky alongside friends in a shared world that grows over time. The studio (founded by Eric Mallon, Martina Qin, and Michael Su) raised a $5M seed round led by BITKRAFT Ventures and GFR Fund with participation from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and took part in a16z's SPEEDRUN gaming accelerator. Loftia is a consumer game company with no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Pop.in
providers.description: Pop.in is a consumer social gaming platform that connects people through real-time multiplayer games including Spades, Hearts, Dominoes, Liar's Dice, crosswords, Pop Quiz trivia, and Just Chatting. Delivered as iOS and Android apps plus a web play surface at play.pop.in, the service reports over 100M downloads and 20M active users with a 4.75+ average rating. The company is backed by 500 Global and was surfaced through its portfolio; it operates a purely consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: TuneCore
providers.description: TuneCore is a Brooklyn, New York based independent music distribution and publishing administration company founded in 2006 (as YourTunes, Inc., rebranded TuneCore in 2008) and acquired by French music company Believe in 2015. TuneCore lets self-releasing artists and labels deliver recorded music to 150+ digital stores and streaming services — Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, TikTok, Tidal, Deezer, Beatport, and others — while retaining 100% of their rights and master ownership, in exchange for a flat annual distribution fee starting at $24.99/year for unlimited releases. TuneCore Publishing Administration registers compositions with performance rights organizations, mechanical rights societies, and digital service providers worldwide to collect songwriter royalties, sync, and neighboring rights income. Additional services include the TuneCore Accelerator artist development program, TuneCore Social (monetization on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts), TuneCore Direct Advance (royalty-backed capital, powered by RoyFi), mastering, and Splits for collaborator revenue sharing. TuneCore operates across 5 continents with local teams in 15+ countries through Believe's global network. There is no current public TuneCore developer API, SDK, or partner portal — an earlier white-label REST/XML "TuneCore Direct" partner API existed circa 2008-2012 (with a community Ruby gem `tunecore_direct`) but is no longer actively documented or promoted. TuneCore's public-facing surface is the artist web app at web.tunecore.com and the support/help center; any current B2B integrations run through Believe's enterprise partnerships.

providers.name: Underdog Fantasy
providers.description: Underdog (Underdog Sports, formerly Underdog Fantasy) is a Brooklyn, New York based sports gaming company founded in 2020 by Jeremy Levine that operates daily fantasy sports, pick'em, and — since 2025 — federally regulated sports prediction markets on its own proprietary technology stack. Its consumer products include Classic Pick'em, Pick'em Champions, Best Ball and other Draft Games, Streaks, Team Picks, and the Underdog Predict prediction-markets exchange, delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps rather than a public developer API. Underdog reached roughly $500M in annual revenue within five years, was valued at $1.2B after a Spark Capital-led Series C in March 2025, acquired CFTC-registered derivatives infrastructure in March 2026, and in July 2026 was the subject of a proposed acquisition by IG Group. The company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its public technical surface is limited to an RFC 9116 security.txt with a PGP key, a Honeybadger-hosted status page covering its API and Stats services, and the Underdog-Inc GitHub organization.

providers.name: Watch Club
providers.description: Watch Club is a mobile streaming and social platform for young adults, built around original coming-of-age teen drama series that viewers watch and then discuss with other fans through polls, episode reactions, and community threads. Its first original series, RETURN OFFER, launches February 2026, with a slate of additional YA series in development. The app is available on iOS and is operated by Kino Technologies Inc. Watch Club is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the consumer sector; it publishes no public developer API surface as of this profile.

providers.name: DICE
providers.description: DICE is a mobile-first live events discovery and ticketing platform founded in London in 2014 by Phil Hutcheon. Through the DICE app (iOS and Android) and dice.fm, fans discover concerts, club nights, festivals, tours and livestreams, buy fee-transparent tickets that live securely in-app, join waiting lists for sold-out shows, and resell tickets at face value to curb touting. DICE also runs a partner business serving venues, promoters, artists and festivals with tools to reach fans, sell tickets and grow their audiences, and owns the Boiler Room brand. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, DICE operates across the UK, Europe and the US. DICE publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, security and legal surface.

providers.name: Gen.G
providers.description: Gen.G is a global esports organization founded in 2017 (originally KSV eSports) that connects the United States and Asia, operating from Los Angeles, Seoul, and Shanghai. It fields professional teams across League of Legends, Valorant, PUBG, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, Brawl Stars, Honor of Kings, Mobile Legends, NBA 2K, Overwatch, Rainbow Six Siege, and EA FC, and runs a youth esports academy program alongside merchandise and fan-engagement businesses. Backed by Canaan Partners among other investors, Gen.G was valued at roughly $250 million as of 2022. It is a consumer esports brand and merchandise operator with a Shopify-based storefront; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: TREBEL Music
providers.description: TREBEL Music (operated by M&M Media, Inc.) is an advertising-sponsored, legally licensed music download and streaming service that lets people download and listen to music offline at no cost. Founded in 2014 by Gary Mekikian, Corey Jones and Luis Soto Durazo and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut with offices in Mexico City, Jakarta, Bogota, Los Angeles and Miami, TREBEL licenses catalog from Universal Music Group, Sony Music Entertainment, Warner Music Group and independent labels, and monetizes through digital advertising, branded experiences, virtual goods and a TREBEL Max tier rather than a conventional paid subscription. TREBEL is a consumer mobile product distributed through the Apple App Store, Google Play and Huawei AppGallery; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Cosm
providers.description: Cosm is a Los Angeles-based immersive technology, media and entertainment company formed in 2020 from the merger of LiveLike VR (now Cosm Immersive) and C360, followed by the acquisition of planetarium pioneers Evans & Sutherland and Spitz. It operates three lines: Cosm Tech (the CX System LED dome, Digistar planetarium software, and end-to-end immersive display systems sold to planetariums, museums and attractions), Cosm Media (immersive content production and licensing through Cosm Studios) and Cosm Venues (the "Shared Reality" experiential venues in Los Angeles and Dallas, with Atlanta, Detroit and Cleveland following). Cosm sells and operates systems and venues rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification. The one API it markets — the Digistar scripting/automation interface, advertised as "the most fully featured API across the planetarium industry" — is documented only inside the customer support portal at partners.cosm.com, which requires a login.

providers.name: Lil Snack
providers.description: Lil Snack is a Manhattan Beach, California games company, founded in 2024, that builds "snackable" daily games and party games — short pop-culture puzzle, word, and trivia titles that refresh every day. It runs its own consumer destination at lilsnack.com (Clue Daily, Scattergories Daily, Swap, DownWords, Pickle, Lite Brite Daily, Wheel of Fortune TODAY, Quiz Climb, Venn, Chain, and more) and also powers games embedded inside partner consumer platforms, citing BuzzFeed, FOX, Hasbro, the Los Angeles Times, Netflix, Peacock, Prime Gaming, Reddit, and Sony. The company reports 40M+ games played and 10M+ players all-time, and monetizes through platform partnerships, sponsorships, and brand licensing. As of this profile Lil Snack publishes NO public developer surface — no API, no documentation portal, no SDKs, no public GitHub organization, and no /.well-known documents; its partner game integrations are arranged through business development rather than self-serve APIs. This API Evangelist profile therefore captures verified company identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: World Golf Tour
providers.description: World Golf Tour (WGT Golf), operated by World Golf Tour, LLC out of San Francisco, is a free-to-play online golf simulation launched in 2008 that recreates more than twenty real championship courses like Pebble Beach, St Andrews, and Bethpage Black using photorealistic imagery, played by over 15 million players on web, iOS, and Android, with virtual equipment from Callaway, Titleist, and TaylorMade and integrations with SkyTrak launch monitors. The company is a Battery Ventures portfolio company and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: 9GAG
providers.description: 9GAG is a Hong Kong-based global entertainment platform founded in 2008 with the mission to "make the world happier." It is one of the largest meme and user-generated humor communities on the internet, distributing funny images, GIFs, and videos across its website and iOS/Android apps to an audience of 150-200 million people and billions of monthly video views. 9GAG operates consumer-facing products (the 9GAG feed, 9GAG Pro subscription, and related community features) rather than a public developer API program; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed company (500 Global, Y Combinator, Freestyle Capital, True Ventures, First Round Capital, Greycroft) and has been enriched with its real public web, policy, and security surfaces. No official public API or developer portal is published as of this enrichment; the community libraries that exist are unofficial and reverse-engineered.

providers.name: Pocket Gems
providers.description: Pocket Gems is a San Francisco mobile games and interactive entertainment studio founded in 2009, employing over 200 people and backed by Sequoia Capital and Tencent. It builds and operates the Episode interactive-storytelling network, Episode XOXO, and the 3D real-time strategy title War Dragons on its proprietary mobile-first Mantis Engine, with products downloaded more than 325 million times. Pocket Gems ships consumer mobile applications rather than a developer-facing API program: there is no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification. Its public developer surface is a GitHub organization and four first-party Apache-2.0 Node.js libraries published to npm under the @pocketgems scope (the internal "Todea" service stack), plus an Episode Writer's Portal used by story authors.

providers.name: Wooga
providers.description: Wooga is a Berlin-based mobile game developer founded in 2009 and a subsidiary of Playtika, specializing in story-driven casual games such as June's Journey, Ghost Detective and Pearl's Peril. Wooga publishes no public API or developer portal, but maintains an active open-source GitHub organization with its atlas Gradle plugin suite for Unity and mobile build automation, published to the Gradle Plugin Portal and RubyGems. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and hv-capital.

providers.name: Tripledot
providers.description: Tripledot Studios (Tripledot Group) is a London-headquartered mobile games developer and publisher focused on data-driven casual games, with chart-topping titles including Woodoku, Solitaire, Duplica, Wordhop, Solitaire Scapes, Sudoku, Spider Solitaire and Blackjack played by more than 25 million daily active users. Founded as an independent studio and named Best Developer at the Pocket Gamer Mobile Games Awards 2023, Tripledot closed an $800 million acquisition of AppLovin's mobile games studio portfolio (ten studios) on July 1, 2025, and is backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Tripledot publishes no first-party developer API, portal or SDKs, but its website ships a real llms.txt and a live, publicly connectable MCP endpoint (the Wix Site Visitor Assistant) for agentic access to site content.

providers.name: Alta VR
providers.description: Alta VR (legally Another Axiom LLC) is a virtual reality game studio behind Gorilla Tag, one of the most-played VR titles ever, and the newer social VR world Orion Drift. The studio builds imaginative, physics-driven multiplayer experiences centered on hand-based locomotion and social play across Meta Quest, Steam, and other VR platforms. It runs an Another Axiom Creator Program for community map-building and content creation, and publishes game code and Unity map-export tooling through its public GitHub organization. Alta VR is a portfolio company of a16z. As a VR consumer game studio it does not currently operate a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program; its developer-facing surface is limited to open-source game code, custom map tooling, and creator resources.

providers.name: CBS (Paramount Global)
providers.description: CBS is the flagship broadcast television network of Paramount Global (NASDAQ: PARA, PARAA). It encompasses CBS Entertainment, CBS News, CBS Sports, CBS Stations (owned and operated), and feeds Paramount+ streaming service. CBS does not publish a consumer developer portal. Partner, syndication, advertising, and distribution APIs are operated privately through Paramount Global's business development, ad sales, and affiliate operations teams.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Book My Show
providers.description: BookMyShow (Bigtree Entertainment Pvt. Ltd.) is India's premier online entertainment ticketing platform, serving as a centralized hub for discovering and booking movies, live music festivals, comedy, theatre, sports, activities, and Video-on-Demand (VOD) streaming. For enterprise partners and event organizers it also provides venue management software, box-office point-of-sale solutions, corporate vouchers, gift cards, and end-to-end event production capabilities. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel; enriched by the enrichment pipeline. No public developer API or portal was found, but BookMyShow publishes an agent-facing llms.txt describing its consumer inventory hubs and B2B services.

providers.name: dreamgames
providers.description: Dream Games is a mobile gaming developer with offices in Istanbul and London that builds high-quality, long-lifecycle casual puzzle games, best known for Royal Match and Royal Kingdom. The company combines technology and creativity to produce polished match-3 titles played by tens of millions of players worldwide, and it was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital. Dream Games operates as a consumer game publisher rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or programmatic API surface. This profile therefore captures the company's real public web, legal, and security surface (website, terms, privacy, careers, help center, and a published security.txt) rather than developer artifacts.

providers.name: Showrunner
providers.description: Showrunner is an AI streaming and animation platform built by Fable Simulation (founded by Edward Saatchi) and billed as the "Netflix of AI." It lets users create and watch AI-generated serialized animated television shows across genres, acting as directors to write, produce, voice, and remix full episodes within simulated worlds such as Sim Francisco, alongside flagship series like Exit Valley. The platform is powered by Fable's proprietary SHOW-2 model and is delivered as a consumer iOS app and Discord community. Showrunner publishes no first-party developer API; its public site is a Wix-hosted marketing property that exposes the standard Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content.

providers.name: Lilith Games
providers.description: Lilith Games (上海莉莉丝网络科技有限公司) is a Shanghai-headquartered video game developer and publisher founded in 2013, known for globally distributed mobile and PC titles including Rise of Kingdoms (万国觉醒), AFK Arena (剑与远征), AFK Journey (剑与远征：启程), Farlight 84 (远光84), Warpath (战火勋章), Art of Conquest (剑与家园) and a portfolio of indie games. The company operates as a consumer game publisher rather than an API platform: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or partner API program. Its public engineering surface is the LilithGames GitHub organization, which open-sources backend and build infrastructure (Go networking and reverse-proxy tooling, build caching, Perforce virtual file system work) rather than client SDKs for a Lilith API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital.

providers.name: Ubiquity6
providers.description: Ubiquity6 was a San Francisco augmented-reality startup ("Capture & Edit Reality") backed by Benchmark, First Round, and Index Ventures. It built Display.land, a multiplayer 3D/AR/VR capture and creation platform, acquired Wavy AR, and was acquired by Discord in June 2021, after which its products were discontinued. Ubiquity6 never published a public API or developer program; its GitHub organization survives as a set of open-source computer vision and React Native forks, and a few internal packages remain on npm under the @ubiquity6 scope.

providers.name: Xperi
providers.description: Xperi Inc. (NYSE: XPER) is an entertainment technology company whose licensed technologies power audio, video, and media discovery experiences across connected cars, consumer electronics, pay-TV, and streaming media platforms. Its brands include DTS immersive audio, HD Radio digital broadcast radio, IMAX Enhanced certification, and the TiVo video platform. Xperi ships its technologies to automakers, device makers, and video providers through commercial licensing and integration programs rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal or API documentation was found, though its TiVo engineering organization maintains an open-source presence on GitHub.

providers.name: Boletia
providers.description: Boletia (Boletia Mexico SA de CV) is a Mexican event ticketing, registration, and access-management platform headquartered in Monterrey, Nuevo Leon. Event organizers use Boletia to create and promote events, sell tickets online, manage attendee registration, assign numbered seating, publish billboards (cartelera) and venue pages, and control event-day access and check-in. The platform spans concerts, comedy and stand-up, sports, expos and congresses, festivals, theater, and workshops across Mexico, and provides the payment and infrastructure backend that powers ticket sales for its event organizers. Boletia is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: All City Network
providers.description: ALLCITY Network (All City Network) is a sports media and podcasting company built on the tagline "Sports Over Everything." It operates a set of city-based sports networks — DNVR (Denver), PHNX (Phoenix), CHGO (Chicago), PHLY (Philadelphia), and DLLS (Dallas) — that produce team-focused podcasts, video shows, and written coverage of local professional and collegiate sports, alongside network-wide shows and NBA/NFL programming. The company reaches fans through audio and video podcasts, memberships, and a merchandise store. It is a Bullpen Capital portfolio company and is not an API provider; it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API, so the API-specific artifacts of the enrichment pipeline are not applicable.

providers.name: Audible
providers.description: Audible is an Amazon-owned online audiobook, podcast, and spoken-word entertainment service. It sells and streams audiobooks, Audible Originals, and podcasts through membership plans and a la carte purchases, delivered via web, iOS, Android, Alexa, and Kindle apps. Audible does not operate a public developer program or documented API — its catalog, library, and playback endpoints are a private internal API consumed by its own first-party apps. Community projects (the mkb79/Audible Python library, audible-cli, and omarroth/audible.cr) reverse-engineer that internal API; none are first-party or officially supported. This profile catalogs Audible's public web, help, and legal surface plus the unofficial client ecosystem.

providers.name: Awa Studios
providers.description: AWA Studios (Artists, Writers & Artisans, Inc.) is a New York-based independent multimedia entertainment company founded in 2018 by comics-industry veterans, including former Marvel editor-in-chief Axel Alonso and former Marvel president Bill Jemas, with media executive Jon Miller as board chairman. AWA publishes original comic books and graphic novels across action, crime, horror, science fiction, and fantasy genres, built around a creator-owned business model that offers favorable terms to writers and artists. The company operates the "Upshot" imprint and a shared "Resistance Universe," runs a direct-to-consumer shop for print and digital titles, and develops film and television adaptations of its properties. AWA received seed-stage funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2018. It is a media and entertainment company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Crystal Dynamics
providers.description: Crystal Dynamics is a AAA video game development studio, best known as the home of the Tomb Raider franchise and its Lara Croft character, and part of the Embracer Group. The studio publishes a consumer-facing marketing website, careers portal, player support center, and news/community hub, but exposes no public developer API program, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub lead; enrichment confirms there is no public API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Donut Media
providers.description: Donut Media is an American automotive entertainment brand and one of the largest automotive channels on YouTube, founded in 2015 by Matt Levin, Ben Conrad, and Nick Moceri. It is best known for original series such as Up to Speed, Money Pit, and HiLow, along with the Past Gas podcast, reaching millions of car enthusiasts through video, social, and audio. Donut monetizes through advertising, brand sponsorships, content licensing, and an extensive Shopify-powered online store selling apparel, hats, and collectibles. The company was acquired by Recurrent Ventures in November 2021. This profile documents Donut Media's public web and commerce surface; the company does not publish a developer API program.

providers.name: Fitetv
providers.description: FITE (fite.tv) is a live sports and entertainment streaming platform that now operates as TrillerTV, run by Flipps Media Inc., a Triller Group Inc company. The service specializes in combat sports and alternative entertainment, streaming boxing, bare-knuckle fighting (BKFC), MMA, kickboxing, professional wrestling, cricket (via the Willow by Cricbuzz channel), soccer, cycling, and motorsports. It advertises thousands of hours of free video, more than a thousand live events per year, and a multi-million-strong fan community, with content delivered through free tiers, the TrillerTV+ subscription, and pay-per-view events across web, mobile, and connected-TV apps. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web surface; no public developer API or documentation program has been located.

providers.name: Hutch Games
providers.description: Hutch Games (Hutch) is a mobile game development studio founded in London with additional studios in Dundee, Scotland and Nova Scotia, Canada. Hutch specializes in free-to-play mobile driving and car games, developing and publishing titles including F1 Clash, Top Drives, and Matchcreek Motors. The studio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer mobile game publisher, Hutch does not currently expose a public developer API or developer program; this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Jam City
providers.description: Jam City is a Culver City, California mobile entertainment company founded in 2010 by MySpace co-founders Chris DeWolfe and Aber Whitcomb (with Josh Yguado), now led by CEO Simon Sim. It develops and publishes free-to-play mobile games across puzzle, casual and narrative RPG genres — including the Cookie Jam and Panda Pop franchises and licensed titles such as Harry Potter: Hogwarts Mystery, Disney Emoji Blitz and Family Guy: The Quest for Stuff — built with partners including Disney and Warner Bros. Games. The company reports over $4 billion in aggregate lifetime bookings and nearly 1.5 billion downloads across studios in Los Angeles, Burbank, San Diego, San Francisco, Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Toronto. Jam City is a consumer games publisher: it distributes through the Apple App Store and Google Play and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Kabam
providers.description: Kabam is a mobile game developer and publisher founded in 2006 and headquartered in Vancouver, Canada, operating as a wholly owned subsidiary of Netmarble. The studio builds free-to-play multiplayer titles for iOS and Android, best known for Marvel Contest of Champions, alongside Shop Titans, Transformers Forged to Fight, King Arthur Legends, and past titles such as Disney Mirrorverse and Fast & Furious games. Kabam operates studios and offices across Vancouver, Montreal, Charlottetown, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Austin, and Seoul. Kabam publishes no public developer program, API reference, or SDK surface; this profile captures its public web, legal, and support properties plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Mobile Premier League
providers.description: Mobile Premier League (MPL) is a mobile skill-gaming and esports platform founded in 2018 and headquartered in Bengaluru, India, operated by Galactus Funware Technology. It distributes a catalog of casual, card, board and fantasy-sports titles inside a single app and runs tournaments and contests around them, reporting more than 100 million registered users across Asia, Europe and North America. MPL historically ran a game-developer program — a Developer Dashboard and a publish-and-monetize SDK at developer.mpl.live, documented at docs.developer.mpl.live — that let third-party studios ship a single build to the MPL app under a revenue-share agreement. That program's hosts no longer resolve, and MPL publishes no public REST, GraphQL, MCP or event API today. Following India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, MPL discontinued real-money gaming in India; www.mplgames.com is the live consumer surface, principally serving the United States.

providers.name: Odyssey Interactive
providers.description: Odyssey Interactive is an independent game development studio focused on building free-to-play, cross-platform, competitive titles set in bright, hopeful, anime-inspired IP. The studio is best known for Omega Strikers, a free-to-play competitive arena game, and its mission is to "ignite the spark of competitiveness that lives within everyone" by creating community-driven games with longevity. Odyssey Interactive was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal — its public surface is its marketing site, a Verified Creators program, downloadable game asset kits, and a Zendesk-hosted player support center. This profile captures the studio's identity and verified public links.

providers.name: Pokelabo
providers.description: Pokelabo (ポケラボ) is a Japanese mobile game development studio founded in 2007 and headquartered in Tokyo. Originally an independent social-game maker, it became a subsidiary of GREE and, as of January 1, 2025, was integrated into WFS (Wright Flyer Studios) under the GREE group. The studio develops and operates smartphone games built on licensed and original intellectual properties, including titles such as SINoALICE and Magia Exedra (Puella Magi Madoka Magica). Pokelabo is a consumer entertainment company and does not expose a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PortalOne
providers.description: PortalOne is a hybrid gaming platform that blends mobile games with live, interactive television-style entertainment, letting players compete inside shows and classic titles such as Atari's Breakout. Operated by PortalOne AS (Norway) and PortalOne, Inc. (United States), the company delivers its experience through native iOS and Android apps rather than a public developer platform. It is a consumer-facing entertainment product backed by Seedcamp and other venture investors; as of this profile PortalOne publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Resolution Games
providers.description: Resolution Games is a Stockholm-based studio building games for virtual, augmented, and mixed reality platforms including Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, and PlayStation VR. Its titles include Demeo, Spatial Ops, Blaston, Bait!, and Ultimechs. The company is venture-backed (Creandum, GV, Partech) and runs a consumer-facing games business. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web properties (blog, support, legal pages) for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Sandbox VR
providers.description: Sandbox VR is a location-based virtual reality entertainment company operating full-body, free-roam VR experiences for groups of friends, families, and corporate teams across 60+ venues in North America, Europe, and Asia. Guests play social, multiplayer VR adventures — horror, action, sports, and family-friendly titles including licensed properties — using motion-tracked suits and headsets. The business spans company-owned and franchised locations, online booking, gift cards, parties/events, and an unlimited-pass subscription. Backed by a16z and Craft Ventures. Sandbox VR is a consumer entertainment operator and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this record captures the company identity and its public web/security posture.

providers.name: Super Evil
providers.description: Super Evil (Super Evil Megacorp) is an award-winning independent video game studio building shared, cross-platform gaming experiences that push creative and technical boundaries. The studio is best known for the MOBA Vainglory and the shooter Catalyst Black, and has shipped licensed titles including TMNT: Splintered Fate and a Rebel Moon game (Blood Line). Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes only a consumer marketing website (Gatsby/Netlify) and social channels; it exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, OpenAPI, developer portal, or status page.

providers.name: Tactile Games
providers.description: Tactile Games is a Danish mobile game studio headquartered in Copenhagen, founded in 2014, that builds and publishes casual free-to-play puzzle titles for iOS and Android. Its portfolio includes Lily's Garden, Penny & Flo, Makeover Match, the Cookie Cats series (Cookie Cats, Cookie Cats Pop, Cookie Cats Blast), and the Simon's Cat games. Tactile is a portfolio company of Index Ventures. It is a consumer game publisher rather than an API producer: it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Voldex
providers.description: Voldex (Voldex Entertainment) is a game developer and publisher founded in 2015 that acquires, operates, and grows platform-leading games on Roblox, including Brookhaven, Driving Empire, and NFL Universe Football, collectively reaching over 140 million monthly players. Its stated mission is to "bring people together through fun," pursuing a focused strategy of selectively acquiring and stewarding enduring Roblox experiences rather than broad portfolio expansion. Voldex publishes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or API documentation surface — it is a consumer games studio whose products run inside the Roblox platform. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; it was reviewed by the enrichment pipeline and confirmed to have no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Volley
providers.description: Volley is a San Francisco voice-AI entertainment company, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that builds voice-controlled and connected-TV games. Its catalog includes hits such as Song Quiz, Yes Sire, and officially licensed titles like Jeopardy!, Wheel of Fortune, and Family Feud, playable on Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Roku, Fire TV, LG, and Samsung TVs. The company is rebranding its consumer surface as "Weekend." Volley operates as a consumer entertainment product studio and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Duetti
providers.description: Duetti is a New York-headquartered music finance and catalog services company founded in 2022 by Lior Tibon and Christopher Nolte that buys music rights directly from independent artists, songwriters and creators. Artists earning at least $2,000 a year from tracks at least six months old can sell masters, publishing shares or a percentage of their royalties for an upfront cash payment — no debt, interest or recoupment — while keeping whatever they do not sell. Alongside the catalog purchases Duetti provides distribution, royalty tracking and claiming, playlisting across a network of owned Spotify playlists, sync placement, paid advertising, influencer and UGC campaigns, and a commissioned remix program. The company has raised more than $435 million, works with 1,100+ music creators, and publishes the Music Economics Report and the Billboard Music Finance Index. Duetti operates artist-facing web applications (DUO onboarding, statements vault, sync portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract as of this profile.

providers.name: ForeVR
providers.description: ForeVR Games is a consumer virtual-reality game studio that brings classic social bar and backyard games into VR. Its catalog includes ForeVR Bowl, ForeVR Darts, ForeVR Pool, and ForeVR Cornhole, built for multiplayer play across Meta Quest, Steam VR, and PlayStation VR2. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. ForeVR is a consumer game publisher with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Mars Reel
providers.description: Mars Reel (Mars Reel Media Corp) is a Los Angeles-based youth sports media and streaming company producing original basketball and soccer documentary series, athlete training content, and original episodic shows (The Vault, Like Mike, Game City). Its Mars Club membership provides premium on-demand video, and its TFIOM (The Future Is On Mars) label runs a Shopify fashion storefront. Mars Reel is a 500 Global portfolio company operating consumer web and streaming products. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or technical documentation; this profile captures its public identity and consumer link surface only.

providers.name: ProbablyMonsters
providers.description: ProbablyMonsters Inc. is an independent video game company headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with a second location in Fort Worth, Texas. Founded in 2016 by former Bungie CEO Harold Ryan, it operates as a parent company that founds, funds and incubates development teams building AAA and AA interactive entertainment — publishing titles including Crimson Moon, Storm Lancers, IRE: A Prologue and Nekome. ProbablyMonsters sells finished games to players through console and PC storefronts; it is not a platform or developer-tools business. It publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API description, and its GitHub organization carries zero public repositories. This profile records that absence with the probes behind it.

providers.name: Sanlo
providers.description: Sanlo is a multi-platform payments and monetization platform built specifically for game developers and studios. Its products let studios run live ops and accept payments outside the walled gardens of the major app stores to reduce platform commission fees: Webshop Builder (a full-stack direct-to-consumer web shop), Web Checkout (accept payments on any website, web shop, or web game), and Unity Checkout (native iOS/Android in-game checkout for Unity titles via a first-party SDK and API, with one-click checkout, fully customizable UI, and creator-code support). Card and payment collection is powered by Adyen underneath. Sanlo also offers game funding to help studios finance user acquisition and growth. The company is backed by Index Ventures and other gaming-focused investors.

providers.name: Legendary Entertainment
providers.description: Legendary Entertainment is a Burbank, California based global media company that owns, produces, and delivers content to worldwide audiences through three divisions: Legendary Pictures (film), Legendary Television and Digital Media (television and digital content), and Legendary Comics. The company builds and licenses media properties aimed at the fandom demographic, with productions that have generated over $20 billion in worldwide box office, including the Dune, Godzilla and Kong Monsterverse, Pokemon Detective Pikachu, Minecraft, and Street Fighter franchises, plus the Monarch: Legacy of Monsters series. Legendary was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IDG Capital. It operates no public developer program: no developer portal, API documentation, or API reference is published, and developer.legendary.com, api.legendary.com, and docs.legendary.com do not resolve. Its only machine-readable public surfaces are an llms.txt link index, an RSS news feed, and an XML sitemap on the marketing site.

providers.name: Religion of Sports
providers.description: Religion of Sports is an Emmy Award-winning sports media and entertainment production studio founded in 2017 by Tom Brady, Michael Strahan and Gotham Chopra, headquartered in Santa Monica, California and operating as The Religion of Sports Media, Inc. The company produces premium non-fiction film, documentary series and branded content that examine why sports matter, distributed through Netflix, HBO, Paramount+, ESPN, Apple TV+, Showtime, Fox Sports and NBC Sports, with titles including Simone Biles Rising, In the Arena: Serena Williams, Made for March, 5-Star and Alex vs. ARod. It raised a $50M Series B led by Shamrock Capital in June 2022 to build a non-fiction studio arm and expand into new formats and non-sports categories. Its public surface is a marketing and press site; the company operates no developer program, publishes no API documentation, and exposes no machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Tyffon
providers.description: Tyffon Inc. is a Japanese immersive entertainment company that combines creativity and technology to deliver memorable XR experiences. The studio builds VR, AR, and mixed-reality attractions - including Corridor, Kaiju Haven VR, Floria, and Island Mirrorge MR - operates the Tyffonium attraction brand, licenses its XR content to entertainment venues across Japan, and released the GARA AR platform app. A Techstars portfolio company, Tyffon publishes no public developer portal or API surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: 1047 Games
providers.description: 1047 Games is an independent video game studio best known for the arena shooter Splitgate and its follow-up title EMPULSE, a free-to-play movement shooter. Backed by Insight Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners, the studio ships games across PC (Steam), PlayStation, and Xbox. As a consumer game publisher it exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, legal, and community surfaces for the API Evangelist network. Added originally as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with live domain-security and identity probes.

providers.name: Bustle
providers.description: Bustle is the flagship lifestyle and culture publication of Bustle Digital Group (BDG), a New York-based digital media company that moves culture forward through premium editorial content, social storytelling, and live experiences. BDG operates a portfolio of eight brands - Bustle, NYLON, Scary Mommy, W Magazine, Inverse, The Zoe Report, Romper, and Elite Daily - spanning lifestyle, fashion, parenting, entertainment, and luxury. The company produces award-winning branded content and campaigns through its BDG Studios and BDGx experiential arm. Bustle is a consumer media publisher rather than an API provider; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead, and no public developer API or specification has been identified on its properties.

providers.name: favorited
providers.description: Favorited is a mobile-first live streaming platform that helps content creators run interactive, real-time shows with their audiences. The app centers on participatory formats — games, giveaways, and community interactions — so that viewers feel like they are playing together with a creator rather than passively watching a broadcast, alongside monetization tools for creators. Favorited ships as consumer iOS and Android apps and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment and monitoring.

providers.name: Funcom
providers.description: Funcom is a Norwegian video-game developer and publisher founded in 1993, headquartered in Oslo with additional studios in Raleigh (North Carolina), Lisbon, and Bucharest. It is best known for online, open-world, and survival titles including Dune: Awakening, Conan Exiles, Age of Conan, and The Secret World / Secret World Legends, alongside published titles such as Metal: Hellsinger, Aloft, Dune: Spice Wars, and Mutant Year Zero. Funcom is majority-owned by Tencent. It was surfaced as a Northzone portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface, so this profile captures company identity, legal/support links, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Futureplay
providers.description: Futureplay is a Helsinki, Finland-based mobile game studio founded in 2015 that develops free-to-play games for a global audience, having released six titles for more than 120 million players including Merge Gardens, Battlelands Royale, and Idle Farming Empire. Backed by Creandum and now part of Plarium, the studio operates in the consumer gaming sector. Futureplay publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal; player-facing support runs through a Zendesk help center, and legal terms are hosted on the Plarium company site.

providers.name: Hooked
providers.description: Hooked is a mobile entertainment company founded in 2015 by Prerna Gupta and Parag Chordia (Telepathic, Inc.) that pioneered the chat-fiction format: bite-sized, suspenseful stories read as simulated text-message conversations. Its flagship Hooked app reached #1 on the App Store and Google Play in more than 25 countries and over 100 million viewers, and the company later launched Hooked TV, a short-form mobile video streaming service. Hooked uses data and AI to predict and produce hit short-form content distributed across its own apps and social platforms including TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat, and YouTube. It is backed by 500 Global, Cowboy Ventures, Sound Ventures, The Chernin Group, Founders Fund, and Greylock. Hooked does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Immersive Gamebox
providers.description: Immersive Gamebox is a London-founded (2018) location-based entertainment company operating indoor gaming venues across the UK, US, Germany, and the UAE. Each Gamebox combines projection mapping, touch screens, motion tracking, and surround sound to deliver fully immersive, interactive games for teams of two to six players in 30-60 minute sessions. Its catalog spans licensed titles built with partners such as Netflix (Squid Game), Aardman (Shaun the Sheep), Rovio (Angry Birds), and Tetris, alongside originals, and the business runs on bookings, party and corporate packages, Game Pass subscriptions, and a multi-unit franchise model. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of index-ventures. It exposes no public web/REST API today; developer collaboration is limited to a Unity-based SDK offered to game studios building titles for the Gamebox hardware platform.

providers.name: Junglee Games
providers.description: Junglee Games is a skill-based online gaming company founded in 2012 by Ankush Gera, operating as an independent subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, which acquired a majority stake in 2021 in a deal valuing the company at more than $440 million. Headquartered in Gurugram with a studio in Bengaluru, the company builds and operates consumer real-money and casual gaming apps for a base of over 150 million users, with flagship titles including Junglee Rummy, the Howzat fantasy cricket and football platform, Carrom Stars, and Junglee Poker. The company positions trust, safety, and fairness as engineering priorities. Junglee Games is a consumer gaming provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documented API program; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and probed security posture for the API Evangelist network. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: mojiworks
providers.description: Mojiworks is a UK-based social games studio, backed by Balderton Capital, that is pioneering a game genre it calls MuGC (Multi-User Generative Creation) — living, collaborative worlds that communities and AI systems build together. Its released titles include Ready Chef Go, Trivia Party, Chef Showdown and Hatch Cats, and it is building its first MuGC world as a persistent, community-shaped city. The company publishes a public AI Ethics Policy committing to licensed training data, environmental accountability, human oversight and content-safety controls. Mojiworks does not currently expose a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Onibi
providers.description: Onibi (Onibi inc.) is a video game studio founded in 2023 by Benjamin Devienne, with a distributed team in San Francisco, London and Bordeaux drawn from Blizzard, Riot, Ubisoft, EA and Rockstar. Its first title is Tomo: Endless Blue, a procedurally generated monster-taming voxel sandbox open world announced for Steam and funded through a Kickstarter campaign plus roughly $6.5M in seed capital from SeaX Ventures, Serena, Octopus Ventures and Pix Capital. Onibi is a consumer game studio, not an API provider: as of August 2026 the game is unreleased and the studio publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification. The Steam page states an intent to keep the game moddable, but no modding API, tooling or documentation has been published yet, so there is nothing machine-readable to catalog.

providers.name: Overtime
providers.description: Overtime is a sports media and entertainment company building disruptive, digital-first sports leagues and intellectual property aimed at the next generation of fans and athletes. It operates branded leagues including Overtime Elite (OTE) basketball, OT7 seven-on-seven football, and OT Select women's basketball, and reaches nearly 100 million followers across social platforms. Backed by a16z, Overtime generates revenue through sponsorships, merchandise, media rights, and brand partnerships, reimagining how Gen Z engages with sports through content-first entertainment.

providers.name: Phoenix Labs
providers.description: Phoenix Labs is an independent video game developer with studios in Vancouver and Montreal, building immersive online worlds and community-driven games. Its titles include the free-to-play action RPG Dauntless and the cozy life-sim Fae Farm. The studio operates player-facing support and account services for its games but does not publish a public developer platform, API program, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Sapphire Ventures and enriched into the API Evangelist network; its API surface is currently none.

providers.name: Pilotly
providers.description: Pilotly is a media and content audience-testing research platform used by studios, streamers, and brands to test films, trailers, series, and advertising with targeted audiences before release. Its managed service pairs clients with expert research managers who handle survey design, audience targeting, and insights synthesis, while a Study Tracker guides each project through five stages (Requested, Setting up, Fielding, Analysis, Complete). Content is fielded through a secure, DRM-protected and watermarked video player across desktop, mobile, and smart TV. Pilotly is a managed-service SaaS with no public developer API surface; clients named on the site include Netflix, Amazon, Sony, Paramount, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Audible. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PlayQ
providers.description: PlayQ is a Los Angeles-based mobile game developer and publisher creating free-to-play games for a global audience, including titles such as Charm King and Treasure Party. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass PlayQ operates a consumer-facing marketing and game-support website with no public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface; player support is routed through per-game Zendesk help centers.

providers.name: Pops
providers.description: Pops is a consumer mobile application, built by Undefined Software, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), that lets users create, remix, and share AI-powered mini games with friends. Every play instantly becomes a funny gameplay/reaction video you can send to friends. Pops is available on iOS and Android and is organized around game categories such as arcade, 3D, racing, sports, puzzles, party, and reaction games. It is an end-user social and gaming product with no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Supersolid
providers.description: Supersolid is a London, UK based mobile game developer and publisher, backed by Index Ventures, that designs and operates free-to-play mobile titles across merge, cooking, simulation, and multiplayer arena genres. Its portfolio includes Cook & Merge, Snake Rivals, Home Street, Food Street, Adventure Town, Super Penguins, and RoPets. Supersolid is a consumer-facing games studio and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web properties (support, careers, terms, privacy) and domain-security posture. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures.

providers.name: TaleMonster Games
providers.description: TaleMonster Games is a fully remote mobile game studio whose mission is to create games that surprise, challenge, and evolve with players. The team is united by a shared obsession for product craft and a deep love for games, and ships casual mobile titles to iOS and Android. Its debut title, Match Valley, is a casual match puzzle game published on the Apple App Store and Google Play. TaleMonster Games publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or technical documentation; this profile captures its public company and product identity.

providers.name: Triumph Arcade
providers.description: Triumph Labs (originally Triumph Arcade) is a consumer entertainment and commerce company that builds mobile apps for competitive, skill-based gaming and collectibles. Its flagship products are Triumph: Play for Cash, a real-money skill-gaming platform, and Rips by Triumph, a live collectibles and trading-card ripping experience. Backed by Multicoin Capital, the company operates consumer iOS apps and publishes no public developer API surface; this profile tracks the company identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: WebComics
providers.description: WebComics (webcomicsapp.com) is a digital comics reading platform for Asian serialized comics, offering a large free library of manhua, manhwa, and manga across genres such as fantasy, romance, action, drama, horror, and slice-of-life. Readers browse trending titles, daily picks, new arrivals, and recent updates on the web and through native iOS and Android apps, while creators publish work through a separate Contribution Studio. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass WebComics exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or webhook surface; it operates as a consumer content application, so this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture rather than an API integration surface.

providers.name: Sirius XM Holdings
providers.description: Sirius XM Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: SIRI) is the leading audio entertainment company in North America, operating a portfolio of subscription, ad-supported streaming, podcast, and advertising-technology businesses. Its flagship satellite radio service SiriusXM serves roughly 33 million paid subscribers, while Pandora delivers ad-supported and premium music streaming to approximately 40 million active users. The portfolio also includes podcast network Simplecast, programmatic audio adtech platform AdsWizz, audio sales arm SiriusXM Media, and Pandora AMP. SiriusXM Holdings was split off from Liberty Media in September 2024, becoming an independent publicly traded company. This holdings-level index points to the operating subsidiaries; the consolidated developer surface is profiled in the `sirius-xm` repository, with no separate corporate developer program at the holding-company level.

providers.name: Azra Games
providers.description: Azra Games is a mobile role-playing game studio founded in 2022 by Mark Otero and headquartered in Sacramento, California. The studio builds RPGs on its proprietary "RPG GameKit" technology, with its flagship title UnGodly, a dark sword-and-sorcery RPG. Azra Games is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a game studio it publishes a public website, news, careers, terms, and privacy pages but does not expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Harmonix
providers.description: Harmonix Music Systems is one of the world's leading independent game development studios, best known for creating blockbuster music and rhythm franchises including Rock Band and Dance Central, alongside titles such as Amplitude, Fuser, DropMix, Audica, Super Beat Sports, and Harmonix Music VR. Founded in 1995 and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the studio was acquired by Epic Games in 2021 and continues to invent the future of music and motion gaming. Harmonix operates a consumer-facing web presence (games, music, community, blog, and press) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Rovio Entertainment
providers.description: Rovio Entertainment is a Finnish mobile game company founded in 2003 and headquartered in Espoo, best known for the Angry Birds franchise and a portfolio of casual and puzzle titles played by hundreds of millions of players worldwide. It operates game studios across Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Canada, Spain, and Turkey, and became part of Sega Sammy Holdings in 2023. Rovio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Atomico and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Rovio publishes a corporate/marketing website but no public developer portal, API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Shibuya
providers.description: Shibuya is a platform for curated short films and the independent creators behind them, describing itself as a home where fans help greenlight the future of film and audiences discover original storytelling. Operated by NotShibuya, Inc. and backed by a16z, Shibuya began as a web3 storytelling experiment and has grown into a community-driven curation platform for short-form film, winning a 2025 Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Innovation in Emerging Media Programming. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Shibuya publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its real public web properties.

providers.name: Shoobs
providers.description: Shoobs is a UK-based online events discovery and ticketing platform focused on urban culture — Afrobeats, R&B, hip-hop, dancehall, comedy, theatre, festivals, brunches and club nights across London and other British cities. Founded as a Y Combinator-backed startup, Shoobs helps fans find and book tickets to events that match their taste, and lets promoters list and sell tickets for urban and Black-British cultural events. The platform pairs an events listing and discovery site with an integrated editorial blog covering artists, concerts and nightlife. Shoobs is a consumer web product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Wildlife Studios
providers.description: Wildlife Studios is one of the world's largest mobile game developers and publishers, founded in Brazil in 2011. It builds and operates free-to-play games played globally, with more than 4.7 billion downloads across a portfolio of over 60 titles including Zooba, Sniper 3D, Tennis Clash, War Machines, and Sky Warriors, and runs a publishing division for third-party studios. Wildlife is a consumer gaming company: its public surface is player-facing games and corporate/careers content, not a developer platform. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bleacher Report
providers.description: Bleacher Report is a digital sports media company headquartered in San Francisco and owned by Warner Bros. Discovery (Turner Sports). Founded in 2007, it delivers sports news, live scores, highlights, video, and community-driven commentary across the web and its iOS and Android applications, spanning the NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, and other leagues. Bleacher Report maintains a public GitHub organization with open source engineering projects but does not publish a public developer API program; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fox Corporation
providers.description: Fox Corporation (NASDAQ: FOXA, FOX) is a US media company spun out of 21st Century Fox in 2019 when the rest of the business was sold to Disney. Per the company website, "Fox Corporation produces and distributes compelling news, sports, and entertainment content through its primary iconic domestic brands" — Fox News Media (Fox News Channel, Fox Business Network, Fox News Digital, Fox News Audio, Fox Weather), Fox Sports (FS1, FS2, Big Ten Network, Fox Deportes, Fox Bet partnerships), Fox Entertainment, Fox Television Stations, and the Tubi Media Group (Tubi free ad-supported streaming, Credible). In May 2024 Fox acquired Mexican sports-betting and casino operator Caliente.mx, expanding its sports-and-wagering footprint into Latin America. Fox does not publish a public developer portal or REST API surface for the parent corporation — programmatic distribution is delivered via per-brand RSS / Atom feeds (Fox News, Fox Business, Fox Sports, Fox Weather), the Tubi Media Group open source projects on GitHub (github.com/Tubitv, 53 public repositories), and direct B2B advertising and content-syndication relationships rather than self-serve API signup. This apis.yml therefore catalogs the public RSS surface, Tubi engineering OSS, and the corporate/brand web properties.

providers.name: Audacy
providers.description: Audacy, Inc. is a U.S. multi-platform audio and entertainment company that operates the country's second-largest radio group alongside the Audacy streaming app, a major podcast network, and the Amperwave audio ad-tech and distribution platform. Formerly known as Entercom (rebranded to Audacy on March 30, 2021), the company filed prepackaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy on January 7, 2024 and emerged on September 30, 2024 as a privately held company after equitizing approximately $1.6 billion of funded debt and reducing total debt from roughly $1.9 billion to $350 million. The current portfolio spans ~230 radio brands across 47 markets, 200+ million monthly listeners, ~2 billion annual podcast downloads, and the Cadence13, Pineapple Street Studios, Podcorn, and BetMGM Network (formerly BetQL) audio brands. There is no public developer API, no published OpenAPI, and no GitHub organization with public repositories; integration is brokered through ad sales, programmatic marketplaces, and the Amperwave platform.

providers.name: 6 Waves
providers.description: 6waves is a global mobile game publisher founded in 2008 and headquartered in Hong Kong, with offices in China, Japan, and the United States. The company partners with independent game developers around the world to publish, localize, and operate social and mobile games, offering culturalization, product guidance, live operations, marketing, platform relationships, customer service and community management, technical support, quality assurance, and VIP management. 6waves is recognized as a pioneer of top-grossing mobile game publishing, particularly in the Japanese market, and is a portfolio company of Insight Partners.

providers.name: AlmostApps
providers.description: AlmostApps is a Sacramento, California sports-gaming studio founded in 2022 that builds free-to-play mobile entertainment experiences for sports fans, blending casual gameplay with real-life sports scores and stats. Its flagship product, Tailgate, is a free-to-play mobile sports entertainment app designed to enhance the game-day experience for casual sports enthusiasts. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Parade Ventures. AlmostApps is a consumer application company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation; only a marketing site with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy is publicly available. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: AutoLotto
