providers.description: AutoLotto, Inc. operates Lottery.com, a mobile platform that lets users in participating US states play official draw lottery games such as Powerball and Mega Millions from their phones, track tickets, view winning numbers, jackpot sizes and draw times, and collect winnings to a linked bank account. Beyond the consumer app, AutoLotto runs a business data-licensing offering that syndicates results and draw data for hundreds of lottery games worldwide to partner digital properties. AutoLotto is venture-backed (500 Global, Pantera Capital) and its parent trades publicly. As of this enrichment pass Lottery.com exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; data access is arranged through a manual "license our data" inquiry form rather than a programmatic surface.

providers.name: Baller League
providers.description: Baller League is a small-sided (six-a-side) football entertainment league and media format founded in Germany that bills itself as "a new era of football, created for the streets by the streets." Teams are captained by professional footballers, influencers, and streamers, with matches played under a fast-paced ruleset and distributed primarily through live streaming and social video (Twitch, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram) rather than traditional broadcast. The organization has expanded from Germany into the United Kingdom and United States and is running its fourth season. It is a consumer sports-media and entertainment brand; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer program. Backed by EQT Ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: BIT ODD
providers.description: BIT ODD is a Helsinki-based mobile game studio founded in 2019 by former Supercell creative leads Lasse Louhento, Taneli Oksama, and Jani Lintunen. The studio hand-crafts casual mobile games driven by feeling and a sense of wonder rather than aggressive monetization, explicitly rejecting ad-spam and dark-pattern design. Backed by Index Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Makers Fund across a EUR 5M seed and a EUR 17M round, BIT ODD is a consumer entertainment company with no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead and carries only the artifacts that can be honestly probed from its public web presence (domain security, legal pages).

providers.name: Clicker
providers.description: Clicker is a consumer-facing streaming guide and discovery platform that helps people find where to watch popular and new movies and TV shows across streaming providers, aggregating title availability from services such as Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, Max, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+, Paramount+, Peacock, Starz, BET+, Philo, and FuboTV into a single searchable catalog. The product is a web application (Next.js) organized around TV Shows and Movies browse and search experiences. Clicker is backed by Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Clicker publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; its only backend surface is a private, robots disallowed internal application API.

providers.name: Closing Theory Studios
providers.description: Closing Theory Studios, Inc. is an independent mobile game studio founded in 2023 and based in Austin, Texas, on a mission to bring the real world into games. Its debut title, Househunt (the officially licensed ZillowGoneWild game), lets the 70 million-plus people who browse Zillow for fun buy, guess prices on, renovate, flip, and manage real houses in a casual mobile experience aimed at "non-gamers." The studio was co-founded by Ankith Harathi and Nitin Rajinikanth and raised a $2.3M round led by a16z GAMES SPEEDRUN, with participation from Powerhouse Capital and angel Seth Sivak (founder of Proletariat, acquired by Blizzard). Closing Theory Studios ships consumer mobile games on iOS and Android and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: couple
providers.description: couple (couple.me) is an AI companion chat platform operated by Fab AI LTD and backed by Slow Ventures. The consumer-facing product lets users create and customize an AI girlfriend, boyfriend, or anime character, then hold personalized text conversations and request AI-generated images from that companion. It offers a free tier with an optional premium subscription. It is a consumer app with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass; this profile captures the company identity and the domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Flickplay
providers.description: Flickplay, Inc. is a Web3 social and gaming company that turns character intellectual property into portable, interactive, and monetizable experiences across user-generated content, social platforms, and real-world retail activations. Its consumer iOS app combines character-based gameplay (blind boxes, spin games, leveling), AR video and GIF creation tools, AI character chat, iOS home-screen widgets, a quest system tying gameplay to e-commerce, and a Fandom Intelligence dashboard tracking fan identity, behavior, and spend. Flickplay is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of mid-2026 the company published a suspension notice, and it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal — this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: FreshPlanet
providers.description: FreshPlanet Inc. is a New York City based mobile game developer, headquartered at 200 Hudson St, New York, NY 10013, best known for the music trivia franchise SongPop. The studio builds free-to-play mobile entertainment titles for iOS and Android, combining licensed music catalogs, social multiplayer play, and live events. FreshPlanet is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As a consumer game studio it does not operate a public developer program or API: it exposes only a marketing site, player support via a Zendesk help center, and standard legal surfaces (Terms of Use and Privacy Policy). This profile captures the studio's real public web and legal footprint for the API Evangelist network; there is no OpenAPI, SDK, or agent surface to enrich because the company publishes none.

providers.name: Good Job Games
providers.description: Good Job Games is a global mobile gaming company founded in 2017 that designs, develops, and operates puzzle and match-3 titles for iOS and Android, including Wonder Blast and Match Villains. The studio publishes its games through the Apple App Store and Google Play rather than a developer API program, and its public web surface is limited to its marketing site, games catalog, careers ("Life at Good Job Games") pages, and legal policies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, SDK, documentation, or API reference was found during enrichment; the artifacts captured here reflect its domain security posture and public web properties.

providers.name: Mad Realities
providers.description: Mad Realities is a creator-powered entertainment network that produces original episodic shows for internet-native audiences, bridging the gap between culture born online and television-level production by partnering with creators. Its Mad Labs arm is an R&D effort leveraging AI and technology to superpower creatives. Backed by Paradigm, the company operates as a consumer media brand and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Mission Control Games
providers.description: Mission Control Games is a mobile game studio building casual puzzle games, co-founded by Kivanc Okutur (CEO) and Murat Gurel (CTO), veterans of the team behind Merge Dragons. Headquartered across London and Istanbul (legal entity Mission Control Games Yazilim Anonim Sirketi), the studio works in small teams to create new casual puzzle sub-genres through rapid iteration and AI-assisted development. It launched publicly in April 2026 alongside a $4M pre-seed round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Arcadia Gaming Partners and e2vc. The company operates a marketing website only and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Mother Games
providers.description: Mother Games is a Brooklyn, New York consumer gaming studio backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of mid-2026 the company is pre-launch: it operates a public waitlist for its debut social title "Le Zoo" and runs a campus ambassador program from its Williamsburg mailbox address (223 Bedford Ave #200, Brooklyn, NY 11211). Mother Games does not currently expose any public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer platform surface — probes of the domain returned 404 for every /.well-known/, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /api, /docs, and /developers path. This profile tracks the company identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead pending any future developer platform.

providers.name: PLAYSTUDIOS
providers.description: PLAYSTUDIOS, Inc. (Nasdaq: MYPS) is a developer and publisher of free-to-play casual and casino-style mobile and social games, including myVEGAS Slots, POP! Slots, MGM Slots Live, myKONAMI, Tetris Block Puzzle, Solitaire, Bingo, and Mahjong titles. Its differentiating platform, playAWARDS, is a loyalty rewards engine that lets players earn real-world rewards from brand partners across gaming, hospitality, dining, and entertainment. The company is headquartered in Las Vegas and went public in 2021 via a business combination with Acies Acquisition Corp. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a dcm-ventures portfolio company; PLAYSTUDIOS publishes consumer-facing games and corporate/investor properties but no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Rigi
providers.description: Rigi (Rigi TV) is an instant-entertainment mobile app that streams quick, captivating, and scroll-worthy short-form video and micro-drama series across genres such as romance, drama, thriller, and suspense. Operated out of HSR Layout in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India and backed by Accel, it delivers on-demand vertical entertainment through its Android app. It is a consumer-facing streaming product; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal surface is currently published.

providers.name: Roboto Games
providers.description: Roboto Games is an independent video game development studio building Stormforge, an open-world survival crafting game where players craft, build, fight, and harness epic storms to survive in a magical fantasy world. The studio was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a consumer game studio, Roboto Games publishes a marketing website, a careers page, and a studio blog, but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface — its player-facing experience is delivered through native game clients (Steam) and community channels (Discord, YouTube, Twitch) rather than an HTTP API. This profile captures the studio's public identity and web properties; no API artifacts are produced because none are published.

providers.name: Season Share
providers.description: Season Share (SeasonShare) is a ticketing technology platform for sports and entertainment venues. Its subscription-pass, last-minute, student, and credit-based products — Pass, Flow, Flex, and LivePass — help teams and venues reach younger fans, capture first-party data, and build recurring ticket revenue. It reports $100M+ in ticket inventory delivered and 1.5M tickets purchased, and is used by 30+ franchises including the Sacramento Kings, New Jersey Devils, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Nashville Predators. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SuperQuickQuestion
providers.description: SuperQuickQuestion (SQQ) is a fan-engagement platform that hosts brief, 60-second one-on-one live video interactions between fans and celebrities, athletes, and musicians. It is web-based with no app download required, uses industry-standard encryption, and removes traditional event logistics (travel, hotels, agent back-and-forth) so talent only needs WiFi and a camera device while fans receive brand- or team-sponsored free access. Early clients include professional sports organizations such as the Washington Wizards, Cleveland Browns, Washington Mystics, Wrexham AFC, and talent like Ric Flair. No public API, developer portal, or SDK surface is currently published; this remains a consumer product profile.

providers.name: turntable
providers.description: turntable (Turntable Labs) is a consumer social-music company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and union-square-ventures. The original Turntable.fm social listening service shut down in 2013 and its domain no longer resolves. The lineage lives on at Turntable Labs, which operates two consumer music products - Hangout (a social music-streaming and group-chat app at hangout.fm / hang.fm) and Turntable (a create-share-and-vibe GenAI music experience). No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation are published for any of these products - this is a consumer application, not an API provider. Enrichment probes (DNS, HTTP, site fetch) confirmed no developer surface as of 2026-07-21.

providers.name: Incite Interactive
providers.description: Incite Interactive is an AI-native gaming studio founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz's Speedrun program, building AI-powered emergent narrative games where the stories players tell matter more than the ones they are told. Its "Everything Story Engine" is an agentic game engine that lets anyone create AI characters and living-world scenarios, powering products such as Embark and Incite Worlds — a roleplaying sandbox of human and AI-driven characters. The founding team are veterans of Zynga, Roblox, and Manticore Games with deep expertise in language models, user-generated content, and live-game operations. There is no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Time Warner
providers.description: Time Warner was a Fortune 500 American multinational mass media and entertainment conglomerate, one of the largest media companies in the world until its acquisition by AT&T in 2018. It operated major brands including HBO, CNN, Turner Broadcasting, Warner Bros., and DC Comics. After the AT&T acquisition it was rebranded as WarnerMedia. In 2022, WarnerMedia merged with Discovery Inc. to form Warner Bros. Discovery. Time Warner did not offer a public developer API platform.

providers.name: KK直播 (KK Live)
providers.description: KK直播 (KK Live) is a Chinese mobile-first video livestreaming and social entertainment platform operated by 杭州米络文化传播有限公司 (Hangzhou Melot Culture Communication Co., Ltd.), part of 米络星集团 (Melot Group), headquartered in Hangzhou with offices in Beijing, Changsha, Xi'an, Shenyang, Los Angeles and Mumbai. Founded in 2012 to fill the gap in mobile livestreaming variety shows, the platform pairs talent and performance streaming with interactive social features — virtual gifting, bullet comments (弹幕), multi-person live connections, PK mini-games, karaoke rooms, outdoor streaming and paid companionship. The company reports more than 100,000 independent streamers, over 600 partner talent agencies and 150 million registered users. Melot Group runs three business lines — entertainment livestreaming, online education and video service solutions — under the KK, 棒直播 and 米乐 brands. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners (启明创投), Sequoia China (红杉资本), CMC Capital (华人文化基金) and Shanda Capital (盛大资本). KK Live is a business-to-consumer product: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Prizeo
providers.description: Prizeo is a charity fundraising platform that runs celebrity-driven online sweepstakes: supporters donate as little as $10 to a participating cause to be entered for a chance to win once-in-a-lifetime experiences and prizes with well-known names in music, sports, and entertainment. Campaigns run on behalf of charities and celebrity partners, donations are processed online (Stripe and PayPal), and winners are selected by raffle under published official rules. Prizeo operates as part of the Charity Network family of fundraising brands (alongside Charitybuzz) and was backed by Battery Ventures. It is a consumer-facing web application; the /api/v1 and /api/v2 endpoints observed on the site are private backends for its own React frontend rather than a documented, public developer API — there is no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or public API program.

providers.name: Future Trash
providers.description: Future Trash is a Los Angeles-based independent, multidisciplinary creative game studio and the developer behind FOAD, a user-generated-content (UGC) native video game franchise. Founded around 2022, the team first built a vertical-slice MVP of FOAD in Unreal Engine 5 and released it in early access on Steam. After Epic Games launched Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) in 2023, the studio pivoted to building FOAD experiences natively inside Fortnite's UGC ecosystem, spanning MOBA, tycoon, and combat modes, while planning to resume the standalone UE5 core game. Future Trash raised a $5M seed round in September 2024 led by TIRTA Ventures with participation from General Catalyst. This profile was surfaced from General Catalyst's portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; Future Trash is a game studio and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: MemeChat
providers.description: MemeChat is an Indian consumer social and creator-economy mobile app from MemeChat Private Limited (Memetech), where users make, share, and compete with memes — including a Face Swap AI feature and a MemeChat keyboard — and earn money when their content goes viral. Marketed as a self-reliant ("Atmanirbhar") Indian app that has crossed five million users, it is backed by 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile is a network stub: MemeChat is a consumer application with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface discovered at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: ThatGameCompany
providers.description: ThatGameCompany is an American independent video game studio founded in 2006 by Jenova Chen and Kellee Santiago, known for emotionally driven, art-forward titles including Flow, Flower, Journey, and the free-to-play social adventure Sky: Children of the Light. The studio focuses on creating timeless interactive entertainment that inspires human connection across all ages. It publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a technology / gaming entity and records domain-security posture from live probes.

providers.name: TMRW Sports
providers.description: TMRW Sports is a sports, media, and entertainment company founded by professional golfers Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, with Mike McCarley as Founder and CEO, focused on building modern, tech-forward approaches to live sports. Its ventures include TGL, a primetime team golf league played in partnership with the PGA TOUR; WTGL, a professional women's golf league; and a professional flag football league launching in partnership with the NFL. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners, TMRW Sports operates consumer sports and entertainment properties and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: BallerTV
providers.description: BallerTV (Baller, Inc.) is a Pasadena, California sports media company that live streams and provides on-demand replays and highlights of youth and amateur sports, including basketball, volleyball, soccer, lacrosse, softball, and football, from thousands of tournaments and showcases nationwide. Subscribers range from families following athletes to NCAA and professional scouts using the footage for recruiting and scouting. The platform includes a Game Finder for locating events, purchasable athlete highlight reels, and BTVision, an AI-powered ball-tracking streaming technology that improves the basketball viewing experience. BallerTV is a consumer streaming product delivered through its website and iOS/Android apps; it does not publish a public developer API or SDK program. This profile was surfaced as an index-ventures portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Cinemark Holdings
providers.description: Cinemark Holdings is one of the largest motion picture exhibitors in the world, operating theatres across the United States and Latin America under the Cinemark, Century, Tinseltown, Rave, and CineArts brands. Cinemark does not currently publish a general-purpose public developer portal; ticketing, showtime, and loyalty integrations are typically delivered through partner agreements and third-party aggregators (Movio, Atom Tickets, Fandango).

providers.name: Touchten
providers.description: Touchten (Touchten Pte. Ltd.) is an award-winning mobile game studio headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia, and an early 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. Its casual games - including Piper's Pet Cafe, Royal Garden Tales, Dessert Chain, Warung Chain Go Food Express, and the Teka-Teki Saku (TTS) crossword series - are published on the App Store and Google Play, are played by millions worldwide, and cater especially to the underserved women gamers market in the US and Europe. Touchten won the Google Play Indonesia Games Contest and received the Forbes Indonesia Rising Global Stars Award. The company publishes no developer portal or public API surface.

providers.name: DAZN
providers.description: DAZN is a global over-the-top live sports streaming service headquartered in London and owned by Access Industries. Launched in 2015 out of the former Perform Group, it streams boxing, football, MotoGP, UFC and other rights to subscribers across more than 200 countries and territories, and has expanded through the acquisitions of Eleven Group, Foxtel/Kayo Sports and ViewLift, alongside the DAZN Bet and DAZN Media brands. DAZN operates a large Node.js microservice estate on AWS and publishes open source engineering tooling (the Kopytko Roku ecosystem, dazn-lambda-powertools) from its GitHub organization, but it runs no public developer program: there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable specification for the consumer platform APIs that power its apps.

providers.name: One More Game
providers.description: One More Game is a fully remote game development studio founded by veterans behind titles such as Warcraft, Diablo, StarCraft, and Guild Wars. The team builds delightful, social online games designed to be played with friends, emphasizing fast iteration and a mission to help players have more fun. One More Game was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. The studio publishes a consumer gaming website, a company blog, careers listings, and a GitHub organization (PlayOneMoreGame) of game-development tooling and forks, but does not currently operate a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Drone Racing League
providers.description: The Drone Racing League (DRL) is a New York-based professional drone racing property founded in 2015 by Nicholas Horbaczewski, staging first-person-view (FPV) races in which pilots fly identical, league-built quadcopters - the Racer series - through three-dimensional courses in stadiums, arenas and landmark venues at speeds above 80 mph. DRL designs its own racing drones, timing and telemetry hardware, produces and distributes its race broadcasts across NBC, Sky Sports, ProSiebenSat.1 and streaming platforms, and operates the DRL Simulator, an FPV racing game on Steam, PlayStation and Xbox that feeds the Swatch DRL Tryouts esports pipeline used to recruit professional pilots. The company was acquired by Infinite Reality (now Napster) in April 2024. DRL publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specification, and as of the 2026-08-04 enrichment pass its primary web properties (thedroneracingleague.com, drl.io) were not completing a TLS handshake.

providers.name: AmpMe
providers.description: AmpMe is a mobile application that synchronizes music playback across multiple smartphones to create a collective, portable sound system. Users connect friends' phones together so their device speakers play the same track in sync, amplifying the audio for parties and gatherings. The app supports streaming sources such as Spotify, YouTube, SoundCloud, and Deezer, and runs natively on iOS and Android. AmpMe was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it is a consumer mobile product that does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.description: Free meme API with 2400+ templates, search, trending, and AI generation

providers.name: Raid Base
providers.description: Raid Base Inc. is a Los Angeles-based game development studio, founded in 2020, building an open-world, sandbox PvPvE game in an original IP where players and crews build reputations through farming, trading, building, fighting, and politics. The team draws from Riot Games, Valve, Blizzard, Microsoft, and Bungie, and the studio has raised roughly $34.4M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), BITKRAFT Ventures, Patron, F4 Fund, and Dreamhaven. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Those Beyond
providers.description: Those Beyond is a fandom entertainment company that merges gaming and community into immersive, location-based and online experiences for fans, gamers, and creators. Built by the Cauldron Co studio and backed by Seedcamp, it runs interactive worlds and events tied to major fandoms (including Invincible- and SCP-branded experiences) alongside a Discord community. Its public surface is a consumer marketing site on Squarespace; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or /.well-known/ discovery documents.

providers.name: FilmTrack
providers.description: FilmTrack is a cloud-based content and rights management platform for the media and entertainment industry, streamlining the intellectual property lifecycle from project inception through distribution. Its software gives distributors and studios a holistic view of the data behind rights, availabilities, contracts, invoicing, licensing, revenue recognition, royalties, and workflow management. Founded in 1996 by Jason Kassin and headquartered in Studio City, California, FilmTrack was acquired by City National Bank in 2019 and now operates alongside Rightsline. Its API-first architecture enables integration with ERP and financial systems such as SAP and NetSuite, and an event bus for change-driven automation. Customers include Lionsgate, Miramax, Focus Features, Starz, and Screen Australia.

providers.name: Light & Wonder
providers.description: Light & Wonder is a leading cross-platform global games company that develops and distributes gaming content across land-based casinos, mobile platforms, and online channels. The company's portfolio includes titles such as Dancing Drums Prosperity, Rainbow Riches, and Gold Fish, and includes subsidiaries SciPlay (mobile social gaming) and Grover Gaming. Light & Wonder operates customer-facing support portals for both gaming and iGaming partners.

providers.name: Project Admission
providers.description: Project Admission is a ticketing technology company serving the live event industry — professional sports teams, leagues, artists, theaters, and venues. It layers on top of existing ticketing systems such as SeatGeek, Ticketmaster, and AXS to expand opportunities around the ticket and capture more value before, during, and after an event. Its platform provides branded storefronts, multi-channel inventory management, bulk ticket distribution, split season-ticket ingestion, and fan-engagement tools including influencer and group-sales programs. Project Admission does not publicly expose a developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its verified public web and security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rebel Girls
providers.description: Rebel Girls is a global media and publishing brand that celebrates inspiring stories about girls and women, empowering young audiences through books, a podcast, a YouTube channel, apparel and accessories, activities, and the Rebel Girls Sport program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Rebel Girls publishes no developer, API, or well-known discovery surface: rebelgirls.com redirects to www.rebelgirls.com and every standard well-known endpoint returns 404, and there are no developer/api subdomains. This profile captures the company's public identity and a live domain-security posture probe; it carries no API artifacts because there is no public API to describe.

providers.name: ToyTalk
providers.description: ToyTalk was a San Francisco conversational AI company founded in 2011 that built voice and chat characters for entertainment, rebranded as PullString in 2016, and was acquired by Apple in early 2019. Its developer platform - the PullString Web API plus Converse and Author tooling for authoring conversational experiences - was shut down after the acquisition. Today pullstring.com and toytalk.com no longer resolve and both domains are parked on Apple nameservers, the github.com/pullstring organization has been deleted, and the only surviving first-party developer artifact is the orphaned pullstring JavaScript SDK on npm. This profile records that historical developer surface; there is no live API.

providers.name: agavegames
providers.description: Agave Games is a mobile game publisher based in Istanbul, Turkey, founded in 2021 by Alper Oner, Burak Kar, and Ali Baran Terzioglu. The company specializes in casual puzzle games played by millions, with titles including Find the Cat, Wonder Link, What The Hex, Soda Match, and Art Block Puzzle across iOS and Android. Backed by Balderton Capital and Felix Capital (Series A, December 2024), Agave Games is a consumer-facing gaming company; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched with a live domain-security probe and identity hygiene.

providers.name: BLAST
providers.description: BLAST is a Danish esports and gaming entertainment company headquartered in Copenhagen, founded in 2016. It produces and operates premier competitive gaming tournaments and leagues (notably Counter-Strike BLAST Premier) and runs the blast.tv streaming and fan-engagement platform, delivering live events, broadcasts, and interactive esports content to a global audience. Backed by Creandum, Heartcore, Maki.vc, and Vaekstfonden, BLAST was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company. No public developer API, portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures verifiable identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Brain Jar Games
providers.description: Brain Jar Games is a fully-remote independent video game studio founded by AAA industry veterans who have shipped franchises including Mass Effect, Dragon Age, RIFT, and Call of Duty. The studio builds bold, vibrant, music-driven action games designed to be shared; its debut title, Dead as Disco, blends kinetic gunplay with rhythm-synced choreography. Brain Jar Games is backed by Menlo Ventures and Transcend, having raised $12.2M across seed funding, and operates a four-day, 32-hour work week with team members across North America, Europe, and Turkey. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks it as a venture-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Las Vegas Sands
providers.description: Las Vegas Sands Corp. is the world's leading developer and operator of integrated resorts, including The Venetian Resort in Las Vegas (divested in 2022) and Marina Bay Sands in Singapore. The company operates in the casino, hospitality, convention, and entertainment industries.

providers.name: Lunar-X
providers.description: Lunar-X (Lunar X) is a global digital content studio that acquires, develops, and operates creator-driven entertainment brands into globally recognized franchises across animation, educational content, functional music, ecommerce, and live events. Its properties include Economics Explained, Theorist Inc, Music Labs, and Lunar Kids, collectively spanning tens of billions of views and over a hundred million subscribers. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and added to the API Evangelist network. As a media/content operator it publishes a marketing website and privacy policy but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: SFX
providers.description: SFX (SFX Entertainment, now operating as LiveStyle, Inc) is a Beverly Hills based global live-events and electronic dance music company. Originally founded by Robert F.X. Sillerman as a roll-up of EDM festival and event brands, the company reorganized as LiveStyle and continues to produce live music experiences, festivals, and fan events under the banner "For the Love of Music." It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company presents a corporate marketing web presence and publishes no public developer, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Viacom
providers.description: Viacom was an American mass media conglomerate that merged with CBS Corporation in December 2019 to form ViacomCBS (later rebranded as Paramount Global). The combined entity, which included brands such as CBS, MTV, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central, BET, Paramount Pictures, Showtime, and Paramount+, was subsequently acquired by Skydance Media and ceased to exist as an independent public company in August 2025. Viacom maintained open source software through its GitHub organization (ViacomInc), including tools for Roku channel development, tvOS UI components, and broadcast calendar utilities. No public external developer API program was offered.

providers.name: Caesars Entertainment
providers.description: Caesars Entertainment is the largest U.S. casino-entertainment company, operating over 50 gaming facilities, hotels, restaurants, and entertainment venues across the country and internationally. The company operates the Caesars Rewards loyalty program and offers gaming, hospitality, dining, entertainment, meetings and conventions, and retail experiences.

providers.name: Airborne Entertainment
providers.description: Airborne Entertainment was a Montreal, Quebec mobile entertainment company founded in 2000 that published and distributed premium mobile content and applications for carrier decks and early smartphones, including games, ringtones, ring-back tones, images, video and informational content, often under licensed consumer brands. The company raised a $22M round in July 2004 with participation from Insight Partners and Verizon, sold a majority stake to Japan's CYBIRD Co., Ltd. in 2005, was taken back by management in a 2008 buy-out, operated afterwards as Airborne Mobile, and was acquired by Bandsintown in October 2010. It no longer operates as an independent company: both airborneentertainment.com and airbornemobile.com are parked domain-sale listings, and the company never published a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as an API Evangelist network history record.

providers.name: fuboTV
providers.description: Fubo (fuboTV) is a live TV streaming service focused on sports, offering more than 100 live channels covering the NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, Formula 1, NASCAR and major broadcast networks (ABC, NBC, CBS, FOX), alongside news, entertainment and on-demand content. The service includes cloud DVR, multi-device streaming and no-commitment monthly plans. fuboTV was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a direct-to-consumer streaming brand and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web, legal, security and identity surface.

providers.name: MoonActive
providers.description: MoonActive is a mobile game developer and publisher best known for the casual titles Coin Master and Pet Master. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a consumer gaming company MoonActive publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; the enrichment pass captured its security and domain posture only (a published RFC 9116 security.txt with a security contact and disclosure page, plus probed TLS/SPF/DMARC).

providers.name: Singularity6
providers.description: Singularity 6 is a Los Angeles-based video game development studio founded in 2018 by a team of experienced developers, several of them Riot Games alumni, with the mission of forging alternate worlds that deepen players' lives. The studio is the developer and publisher of Palia, a free-to-play community simulation MMO where players build a cozy life, craft, farm, fish, and explore a shared social world with friends. Palia launched into open beta on PC and Nintendo Switch and has grown to millions of registered players. Singularity 6 was acquired by Daybreak Game Company in 2024. The company operates a consumer gaming business and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile documents the company's public web presence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: KAMI
providers.description: KAMI (Çizgi Studio) is a next-generation transmedia entertainment platform out of Turkey that lets a community read, write, and live inside stories. The mobile app and web platform offer thousands of original webtoons, comics (çizgi roman), novels, and AI-character chat across genres like romance, thriller, fantasy, and horror, plus vertical drama viewing. Community-validated narratives are measured through read rates, micro-transactions, and engagement, then graduate into vertical-drama production and licensable intellectual property — a "story IP engine." KAMI is a consumer product (2.5M+ users) with no public developer API; it is part of the wearekami.com ecosystem and a 500 Global Creators Ventures portfolio company, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Darewise
providers.description: Darewise Entertainment is a European game studio founded by AAA industry veterans — game director Benjamin Charbit (Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag) and engine tech lead Samuel Kahn (Ubisoft Snowdrop, Crytek CryEngine) — with offices in Paris, London and Barcelona. It builds Life Beyond, a free-to-play sci-fi MMO on Unreal Engine 5 set on the alien world Dolos, combining Web3 asset ownership (NFTs and ERC-20 tokens) with player-driven settlement and governance. Animoca Brands announced the acquisition of a majority stake in April 2022, and the studio now trades as Life Beyond Studios. The original darewise.com website last served content in April 2025 and the host now refuses TCP connections on 80 and 443. Darewise publishes no API, developer portal, or API documentation of any kind; the only machine-readable developer artifact it has ever released publicly is an open-source AsyncAPI generator template that emits Unreal Engine C++ from an AsyncAPI 3.x document, published to npm under its own scope.

providers.name: Elsewhere
providers.description: Elsewhere (Elsewhere Communities Inc.) is a San Francisco based video game studio founded in 2024 by Paul Sawaya, previously co-founder and CTO of Human Interest. The studio was part of cohort 001 of a16z SPEEDRUN, the Andreessen Horowitz accelerator for games and interactive media. Elsewhere describes itself as "a new kind of video game studio emboldened by the desire to rethink the industry", treating artificial intelligence as a normal technology and building games that use generative AI in a humanistic direction rather than a dystopian one. The studio previously worked on a multiplayer roguelike — games "that feel like an adventure you go on with your friends, and the adventure is never the same twice" — and is currently building something new. Elsewhere is a consumer game studio with no public developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no API, no developer portal, no SDKs, and no machine-readable discovery documents.

providers.name: First Day Entertainment
providers.description: First Day Entertainment Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California game studio building AI-powered games, founded by Stephen Gou (formerly a founding engineer at Cohere) and Mike Mei, and funded by the a16z SPEEDRUN accelerator (batch 002) and MiraclePlus. The studio ships two titles - Heroes of Magic & Cards, a poker deckbuilding roguelike distributed on Steam, and Mana Land, a single-player RPG in which players adventure alongside conversational AI companions, published on itch.io. First Day Entertainment is a consumer games company; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Ranker
providers.description: Ranker is a consumer internet company that runs ranker.com, a crowdsourced ranking and voting platform where users vote on and create rankings across pop culture, entertainment, film, TV, music, food, sports, and other consumer topics. Its business arm licenses "Ranker Insights" audience-intelligence and opinion-graph data - drawn from more than 1.5 billion votes, 115 million voters, and 260,000 rankings - to brands, agencies, publishers, and for AI/LLM training. Ranker does not publish a public, self-serve developer API; a private api.ranker.com powers the site and its robots.txt prohibits automated scraping and AI/LLM training use. Data access is sales-led via business.ranker.com. Backed by Bullpen Capital and DCVC.

providers.name: Second Dinner
providers.description: Second Dinner is an independent, remote-first video game studio headquartered in Irvine, California, founded in 2018 by a group of former Blizzard Hearthstone developers including Hamilton Chu, Ben Brode, Yong Woo, Jomaro Kindred and Michael Schweitzer. Its debut title, MARVEL SNAP, is a fast-paced digital collectible card game built in Unity that won Mobile Game of the Year at both The Game Awards and the DICE Awards along with an Apple Design Award, and the studio has since been reported to be building its next title on the Godot engine. Second Dinner raised a $100M Series B led by Griffin Gaming Partners in January 2024. The studio ships consumer games rather than developer platforms: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification, and its public engineering footprint is a small GitHub organization of Unity build and test tooling forks.

providers.name: Unikrn
providers.description: Unikrn was an esports betting and entertainment company founded in November 2014 by Rahul Sood and Karl Flores, headquartered in Seattle and backed by investors including Mark Cuban, Ashton Kutcher, 500 Global, and Pantera Capital. The platform offered real-money and token-based wagering on competitive video game tournaments (CS:GO, League of Legends, Dota 2, and more) and ran a $30M ICO for its UnikoinGold (UKG) cryptocurrency in 2017, which it later disabled as part of a 2021 SEC settlement. Unikrn was acquired by Entain in August 2021, and the unikrn.com betting site was permanently closed on October 20, 2023. The domain now serves only a farewell notice; the company publishes no APIs, developer portal, or public technical artifacts.

providers.name: FloSports
providers.description: FloSports is an Austin, Texas-based direct-to-consumer sports media and live-streaming company founded in 2006 by brothers Martin and Mark Floreani. It operates a network of vertical properties (FloWrestling, FloTrack, FloGrappling, FloRacing, FloHockey, FloRugby, FloFootball and more) that deliver live and on-demand event streaming, original programming, news, rankings, and results for underserved and passionate sports communities through a subscription model. FloSports surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures; enrichment probing found a consumer streaming site with no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI, well-known discovery documents, or SDK program at this time.

providers.name: Rovio
providers.description: Rovio Entertainment is a Finnish mobile games company best known for the Angry Birds franchise. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Espoo, Finland, Rovio operates multiple game studios and became part of Sega in 2023. It is a consumer entertainment company; its public web presence covers games, careers, press, and support, and it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Taiyaki Studios
providers.description: Taiyaki Studios is a Tokyo-based startup working to redefine how anime is consumed, delivering stories that are immediate, engaging, and satisfying. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Polychain Capital in the DeFi/NFT (web3) sector, the studio pairs anime content production with web3 and AI technology and creator-community building. As of this enrichment pass Taiyaki Studios publishes only a marketing website (taiyakistudios.com) and a contact email; it exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Theorycraft Games
providers.description: Theorycraft Games is an independent video game studio backed by a16z, best known for developing SUPERVIVE, a free-to-play hero shooter / MOBA-battle-royale hybrid. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer game and community presence but no public developer API, developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; the corporate site is in maintenance mode.

providers.name: Topgolf Callaway Brands
providers.description: Topgolf Callaway Brands is a global golf and entertainment company that designs, manufactures, and sells golf clubs, balls, apparel, and accessories under the Callaway, Odyssey, OGIO, TravisMathew, and Jack Wolfskin brands, and operates Topgolf entertainment venues and the Toptracer ball-tracking technology. Topgolf Callaway Brands does not publish a single public developer API portal, though Toptracer ball-tracking technology is licensed to driving ranges through a separate commercial program.

providers.name: Viki
providers.description: Viki (Rakuten Viki) is a global video streaming service specializing in Korean dramas, Chinese dramas, and other Asian television shows and movies, subtitled into more than 200 languages by a community of volunteer contributors (the name is a portmanteau of "video" and "wiki"). Founded as a startup backed by 500 Global, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and CRV, Viki was acquired by Rakuten in 2013 and now operates as part of Rakuten's media portfolio. The consumer product streams licensed content on web, mobile, and connected-TV apps, funded by advertising and a Viki Pass subscription. Viki does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; it exposes an internal application API (api.viki.io) that powers its own clients and requires app credentials, and a community contribution platform for volunteer subtitlers and segmenters. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with the honest finding that there is no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Discovery Communications
providers.description: Discovery Communications was a global media company providing original and purchased programming across multiple distribution platforms before merging with WarnerMedia in 2022 to form Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), a leading global media and entertainment company whose portfolio spans HBO Max, Discovery Channel, CNN, Warner Bros. film studios, DC, Food Network, HGTV, and other television, film, and streaming brands. No public developer APIs are documented at the corporate level; technical and partnership inquiries are handled at the individual brand or business-unit level.

providers.name: Dream11
providers.description: Dream11 is India's largest fantasy sports platform, operated by Sporta Technologies Private Limited and part of the Dream Sports group founded in 2008 by Harsh Jain and Bhavit Sheth and headquartered in Mumbai. Launched as a freemium fantasy game in 2012, it lets 140 million-plus users draft virtual teams and compete in free and paid contests across cricket, football, kabaddi, basketball and hockey, scoring on the real-world performance of the athletes they pick. Dream11 is a consumer, mobile-first product with no public consumer API program; its engineering organization does maintain public open-source infrastructure (Kong rate-limiter and circuit-breaker plugins, the Odin deployment tool) on GitHub and publishes an engineering blog.

providers.name: Filmgrail
providers.description: Filmgrail is an Oslo, Norway based software company offering an AI-powered digital platform for cinema operators. Its product suite bundles a cinema content management system (CMS), native iOS and Android mobile apps, branded cinema websites, and marketing and analytics tooling into a single managed offering, with a loyalty system, festival platform, push notifications, and a planning tool layered on top. Filmgrail markets these capabilities as a way to automate cinema operations and grow digital ticket sales and moviegoer engagement, and describes API-based integration between its platform and cinema point-of-sale systems, websites, and mobile apps. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from Oslo, Norway and Delaware, USA. Filmgrail does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Headgum
providers.description: Headgum is an American comedy podcast network founded in 2015 by Marty Michael, Amir Blumenfeld, and Jake Hurwitz, with studios in Los Angeles and New York. It produces and distributes premium comedy and entertainment podcasts including Doughboys, Not Another D&D Podcast, Dead Eyes, Hey Riddle Riddle, and Why Won't You Date Me?, and operates Gumball, a host-read podcast and YouTube advertising marketplace that lets brands buy ads directly from creators. Headgum is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Headgum publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Playback
providers.description: Playback (playback.tv) is a mobile-first live streaming platform backed by Khosla Ventures, where creators broadcast live streams, audiences watch and interact in real time, and streamers earn through the platform's monetization program. The consumer product is organized around streaming, watching, earning, and community guidelines. As of this enrichment pass Playback publishes a consumer web/app experience and a Notaku-powered help center but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented developer surface; this profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment. The company operates through its publishing labels: Rockstar Games (Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption), 2K (NBA 2K, Borderlands, Civilization, BioShock, Mafia), Private Division, and Zynga (mobile games). Headquartered in New York City, Take-Two is a Fortune 500 company with studios across North America, Europe, and Asia. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Audio Up Media
providers.description: Audio Up Media is a Los Angeles based podcast studio, music company and audio entertainment network founded in 2020 by Jared Gutstadt, the founder of Jingle Punks. The company develops and produces scripted and unscripted audio series, original music IP and branded audio campaigns, and adapts that intellectual property into television, film and live formats. Its catalog includes scripted titles such as Strawberry Spring, Make It Up As We Go, Where the Bodies Are Buried and Maejor Frequency, alongside branded case-study work for consumer brands. Audio Up is a content studio rather than a software platform: it publishes a marketing site and distributes its shows through third-party podcast platforms, and does not operate a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of its own.

providers.name: Boxee
providers.description: Boxee, Inc. was a New York and Tel Aviv based consumer media company founded in 2007 by Avner Ronen, Tom Sella, Idan Cohen, Gidon Coussin and Roy Vulcan. Its cross-platform media-center software began as a fork of the open-source XBMC project and bridged local media libraries with internet streaming sources. Boxee shipped a Python-based application API in April 2009 that let third parties build Boxee apps in Python with XML-defined interfaces, distributed through the Boxee app directory and documented at developer.boxee.tv. Hardware followed with the D-Link Boxee Box (2010) and Boxee TV with a cloud DVR service (2012). Backed by Union Square Ventures and Spark Capital, Boxee was acquired by Samsung Electronics in July 2013; the cloud DVR was shut down on 10 July 2013 and Samsung wound down the Boxee team in 2015. The company is defunct and no API surface, developer portal, or documentation remains reachable.

providers.name: DIVE studios
providers.description: DIVE Studios is a global K-entertainment media platform that produces original shows, podcasts, and short-form social content, reaching over 135M Gen Z and Millennial fans and 5B+ lifetime views. The company operates two commercial arms: DIVE Media, which sells advertising and branded content across its podcast, video, and social network, and DIVE Agency (DIVE X), which builds creator, influencer, and celebrity marketing campaigns for global brands connecting with K-culture audiences. It publishes an llms.txt describing its pages but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or portal. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hungama

Hungama.com offers trending web series, popular movies, Hungama Originals, music, podcasts, audiobooks, and audio stories across Hindi, Bollywood, Punjabi, and regional Indian content. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Hungama publishes a public LLM Access Policy (llms.txt) governing how AI systems may crawl, summarize, and reference its content, but exposes no public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: Kobalt Music
providers.description: Kobalt Music Group is a music services company providing publishing administration, neighbouring rights and recordings services for songwriters, artists, publishers and rights holders. It collects, matches and accounts for royalties across streaming and digital platforms, reporting to clients through its own portals rather than a public developer program. Kobalt's rights and content management platform is operated by KTech, its technology arm, which processes the micro-transaction royalty data behind Kobalt Music Publishing and AMRA, the global digital collection society. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass Kobalt publishes no public API, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification; the only public machine-readable surface found was an RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Light Chaser Animation Studios
providers.description: Light Chaser Animation Studios (追光动画) is a Chinese computer-animation film studio founded in March 2013 by Gary Wang (王微), founder and former CEO of the video platform Tudou, and headquartered in Beijing. The studio produces original CG animated feature films for the Chinese domestic market, drawing on Chinese mythology, literature and history. Its released titles include Little Door Gods (小门神), Tea Pets (阿唐奇遇), Cats and Peachtopia (猫与桃花源), White Snake (白蛇：缘起), New Gods: Nezha Reborn (新神榜：哪吒重生), White Snake 2: Green Snake (白蛇2：青蛇劫起), New Gods: Yang Jian (新神榜：杨戬) and Chang An (长安三万里). Light Chaser is a film-production company rather than a technology vendor: its public web presence is a bilingual WordPress marketing and recruiting site at zhuiguang.com, and as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind.

providers.name: PKO Inc.
providers.description: PKO is a collective and investment group operating at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Describing itself as a community of founders, creators, execs, artists, angels and investors with more than 700 members, PKO runs online and offline networking events, mixers and collaborations, and invests in startups across metaverse, virtual worlds, VR/AR, web3 (crypto, NFTs, DAOs), the creator economy, gaming and esports, social media, platforms, marketplaces, communities, streaming video, and content and media. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. PKO publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface; founders submit pitches by email.
