providers.name: UTURN
providers.description: UTURN Entertainment is a Saudi Arabian digital media and entertainment company founded in 2010 that has grown into the largest Arabic Multi-Channel Network (MCN) in the MENA region. It produces original digital content — comedy sketches, gaming (Saudi Gamer), women's lifestyle (Unseen), sports (MLM), and MMA (MMAnia) shows — distributed across YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, and other social platforms, and offers content creation, sponsored content, branded content, and digital production services to brands. A 500 Global portfolio company, UTURN publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Adim
providers.description: Adim is an entertainment-technology and web3 media company co-founded in 2022 by It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia creator Rob McElhenney alongside Richard Rosenblatt, Chase Rosenblatt, Melissa Kaspers, and Spencer Marell. Adim invites a community of storytellers, writers, and fans to collaboratively create, develop, and co-own a new generation of intellectual property — stories, characters, and narrative universes known as the Adimverse — rewarding contributors with ownership stakes and a say in how the community is governed. The company raised a $5M seed round led by Chris Dixon of a16z crypto. Adim is a consumer creative platform rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Liberty Media
providers.description: Liberty Media Corporation is a media and entertainment holding company headquartered in Englewood, Colorado, owning interests in a portfolio of assets across media, entertainment, and sports. Its primary holding is the Formula One Group, which encompasses Formula 1 racing operations and MotoGP motorcycle racing, alongside investments in companies such as Liberty Broadband, QVC Group, Atlanta Braves Holdings, and Liberty Live Holdings.

providers.name: Methodical Games
providers.description: Methodical Games is an independent AAA game development studio building award-winning multiplayer games, describing itself as "built by developers, for developers." Founded by veterans of Infinity Ward, Respawn Entertainment, Epic Games and Santa Monica Studio, its lean team has shipped and shaped franchises including Call of Duty, Titanfall, Apex Legends, Fortnite, Gears of War and God of War Ragnarok. The studio emphasizes a developer-driven process of fundamentals, quick iteration and collaboration to craft immersive, long-lived multiplayer experiences. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a game studio it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web presence.

providers.name: PaceMaker
providers.description: PaceMaker is the consumer DJ application from Pacemaker Music AB, a Swedish startup and 500 Global portfolio company, that lets anyone mix and mash millions of tracks on iPhone and iPad. It connects to streaming catalogs such as Spotify, includes an AI DJ that suggests matching tracks and beat-matched transitions, and lets users crop and blend songs at phrase, bar, and beat precision to record and share their own mixtapes. Pacemaker is a mobile end-user product; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal, and its domain (pacemaker.net) currently serves a WordPress marketing blog.

providers.name: Smule
providers.description: Smule is an American consumer music technology company whose flagship social singing and karaoke app lets people perform solos, duets, and group songs and collaborate with other singers around the world in real time. Launched on iOS in 2012 and on Android in 2013 under the name "Sing! Karaoke," the app grew to tens of millions of monthly active users. Smule Inc. is headquartered in San Francisco and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Shasta Ventures. Smule publishes no official public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Caffeine
providers.description: Caffeine was a social broadcasting and live-streaming platform founded in 2016 by former Apple designers Ben Keighran and Sam Roberts, and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Greylock Partners. Built on a proprietary WebRTC-based real-time video distribution network, Caffeine positioned itself as a low-latency, social-first alternative to Twitch for gaming, entertainment, and — in its later years — live sports, partnering with roughly 200 sports organizations and reaching tens of millions of monthly users. The company published open-source broadcasting tooling under its caffeinetv GitHub organization (libcaffeine, caffeine-rtc, an OBS plugin, and the CaffQL GraphQL code generator) but never shipped a public, documented developer API program. Caffeine announced it was ceasing operations, and its web presence is now a shutdown notice; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead and is archival rather than an active, integrable API provider.

providers.name: Hasbro
providers.description: Hasbro is a global play and entertainment company committed to making the world a better place for children and their families through brands and franchises including NERF, MAGIC: THE GATHERING, MY LITTLE PONY, and TRANSFORMERS. This repository tracks public APIs, developer resources, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Hasbro. No public developer APIs have been published at this time.

providers.name: Inkitt
providers.description: Inkitt is a data-driven storytelling and self-publishing technology company that runs a reading and writing community (inkitt.com) and the paid serialized-fiction reading app Galatea. It uses reader-engagement analytics and algorithms to discover promising manuscripts from independent authors and develop the most popular into commercial fiction and adaptations across its Inkitt and Galatea platforms. Founded in 2013 and backed by Earlybird, HV Capital, Khosla Ventures, Kleiner Perkins and Speedinvest, Inkitt operates consumer mobile and web reading products rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, domain-security, and GitHub surface.

providers.name: Lego
providers.description: The LEGO Group is a Danish toy company and the world's largest manufacturer of interlocking plastic building bricks. The company extends its brand across video games, theme parks, movies, educational products, and licensed sets for children and adults. LEGO does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; consumer-facing systems and partner integrations are closed. A public GitHub organization hosts internal engineering tooling and open-source contributions.

providers.name: MGM Resorts International
providers.description: MGM Resorts International is a global entertainment company with national and international locations featuring best-in-class hotels and casinos, state-of-the-art meetings and conference spaces, and dining and entertainment venues. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for MGM Resorts International.

providers.name: Movielala
providers.description: MovieLaLa Inc was a San Francisco movie-discovery and social-video startup (500 Global portfolio, founded 2012) best known for its GIF maker and a MovieLaLa Video Player. The only developer surface it ever published was a client-side JavaScript embed API for that player (a drop-in replacement for the YouTube IFrame API, loaded from assets-embed.movielala.com), documented in the github.com/movielala GitHub org. The company is now defunct — its last public code activity was 2016 and the gif-maker repo redirects to gifmaker.io. The movielala.com domain has lapsed and is currently repurposed by an unrelated third party (an Indonesian gambling site), so it no longer represents the company and is not wired as a website here. No REST/OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or hosted API surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: NBC
providers.description: NBC (National Broadcasting Company) is a major American commercial broadcast television network and a subsidiary of Comcast through NBCUniversal. NBC produces news (NBC News, Today), entertainment, late-night, and sports programming (Sunday Night Football, Olympic Games). NBC and parent company NBCUniversal do not publish a public developer portal. Programmatic advertising APIs (NBCUniversal One Platform) and streaming partner integrations (Peacock) are offered only through direct sales relationships rather than self-serve developer signup.

providers.name: Pahdo Labs
providers.description: Pahdo Labs is a venture-backed consumer game studio (an a16z portfolio company) building anime-inspired action-RPG and world-creation experiences. Its public engineering footprint is a game-technology stack rather than a public API product: the pahdolabs GitHub organization publishes forks and modules for the Godot game engine (including a React loader for Godot, a prediction-and-rewind network synchronizer, a Tracy profiler integration, FMOD audio, GodotSteam, and FishNet networking). As surfaced from an a16z portfolio harvest, Pahdo Labs does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, hosted MCP server, SDK for third-party integration, or a documented public API surface at this time. This profile captures the company's real identity and open-source game-engine tooling for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Paramount
providers.description: Paramount is a global media and entertainment company producing premium content and experiences for audiences worldwide, encompassing film, television, and streaming through brands such as Paramount Pictures, CBS, Nickelodeon, MTV, Comedy Central, BET, Paramount+, and Pluto TV.

providers.name: Sofar Sounds
providers.description: Sofar Sounds curates secret, intimate live-music gigs in living rooms, small venues, and unexpected spaces in hundreds of cities around the world. The company connects independent and emerging artists with attentive local audiences through a mobile-first ticketing and events platform, and works with hosts who lend their spaces for the shows. Sofar operates a consumer-facing website and apps rather than a public developer program; probing its surface confirmed no documented public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI. It runs a real GitHub organization (github.com/sofarsounds) of internal engineering repositories, and its production backend is served from api.sofarsounds.com (Heroku), but neither exposes a published, documented API for third-party developers.

providers.name: Tally Labs
providers.description: Tally Labs is a Web3 media and entertainment company founded in 2021 and headquartered in the United States. It is best known for creating and operating Jenkins the Valet, a fictional character and NFT project built around Bored Ape Yacht Club #1798, and for the community-generative NFT novel "Bored & Dangerous," set in the fictional world of Azurbala and written with New York Times bestselling author Neil Strauss. The company builds characters, narratives, and interactive storytelling tools intended to let creators turn their imaginations into content. Tally Labs raised a $12M seed round in May 2022 led by a16z crypto. As a Web3 media/IP company it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 555 Comic
providers.description: 555 Comic is an interactive storytelling and virtual-influencer studio founded by Ben Watanabe. It runs casts of anime-styled virtual characters — such as @CRC_Luna — who publish real-time alternate-reality-game (ARG) stories across TikTok, Twitter/X and Instagram, letting fans create original characters (OCs) and interact with official storylines across four interconnected fictional worlds: Conspiracy Research Club, All Night Arcade, The Convenience Store, and a Paranormal Research Club. Stories unfold in real time on "Poppy-valley Standard Time," with fans participating through social comments. 555 Comic is a Techstars Music portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe of its web host.

providers.name: 7k7k
providers.description: 7k7k (7k7k.com) is a Chinese online casual gaming portal operating a consumer-facing website that aggregates hundreds of free browser-based mini games across action, role-playing, strategy, puzzle, and two-player categories. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The 7k7k property is a consumer web destination and publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or developer documentation; enrichment probes confirmed no OpenAPI, no .well-known discovery documents, and no security-disclosure or trust-center program at this time.

providers.name: 88rising
providers.description: 88rising (stylized 88 with a rising arrow) is an American mass media company and record label founded in 2015 by Sean Miyashiro, headquartered in Los Angeles and New York with a division in Shanghai. It describes itself as a hybrid management, record label, video production and marketing company, and is known for building a global platform for Asian and Asian American artists including Rich Brian, NIKI, Joji and Keith Ape. Beyond recorded music it operates the Head in the Clouds festival franchise and the 88 Night Market live and commerce brand. It is a media and entertainment company rather than a software company: it publishes no developer program, no public API documentation and no machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: All Def Digital
providers.description: All Def (formerly All Def Digital) is a YouTube-focused digital content studio founded by Russell Simmons that produces unscripted original programming for Gen Z, Millennial, and multicultural audiences across comedy, food, hip-hop, and culture. Its owned-and-operated channels have amassed 15M+ fans and more than 2 billion video views, and it produces branded content for partners including Sprite, Snickers, Hyundai, Lexus, and McDonald's. All Def is a portfolio company of a16z, surfaced in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Angelic
providers.description: Angelic (Angelic: Dark Symphony) is a dark, story-rich cinematic turn-based Strategy-RPG from Angelicore Game Studios, where players lead neo-human angels through tactical missions, impossible choices, and cosmic horror. Originally launched as a Web3 / metaverse gaming project backed by Pantera Capital, the title is now distributed as a premium PC game on Steam and the Epic Games Store. Angelic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface as of this profile; it is a consumer game studio rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Ares Interactive
providers.description: Ares Interactive is a game developer and publisher founded in 2024 by veteran industry leaders, operating studios in San Francisco and Berlin. The company builds player-first games designed to evolve with their communities and grow into enduring franchises, with a current portfolio that includes Baseball Hits, Heroes vs. Hordes, and The Walking Dead: Aftermath. Ares Interactive is backed by General Catalyst and was added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer/gaming portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and careers website but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: baoyugame
providers.description: baoyugame (Guangzhou Baoyou Network Technology) is a Chinese game development and publishing studio founded in 2011 and headquartered in Guangzhou, focused on the research and development of mobile games and web (browser) games. Its founding team came from established studios including NetEase, and it operates multiple internal game studios with a development team of roughly 100 people, shipping turn-based RPG, ARPG, and strategy titles. The company is venture-backed, appearing in the portfolios of Qiming Venture Partners, Morningside Venture Capital, and Jiuhe Capital. baoyugame publishes a consumer game website only and exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface, so this profile carries company identity rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Beast Industries
providers.description: Beast Industries is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of social-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: creator-economy. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Beek
providers.description: Beek was a Spanish-language audiobook and ebook streaming platform serving Latin America and Spain, backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners. At its peak it reached over 4 million users who streamed nearly 200 million minutes of audio content, including its exclusive Beek Originals catalog. The service has since shut down: Amazon's Audible acquired a significant portion of the Beek Originals catalog, and Beek now redirects listeners to Audible to continue their libraries. Beek ran a private backend service (api.beek.io) but published no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation, so it has no consumable API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Big Fish Games
providers.description: Big Fish Games is a casual-games publisher and digital storefront offering downloadable and online casual, hidden-object, match-3, puzzle, card, and social-casino titles for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. Founded in Seattle in 2002 and now part of Aristocrat's Pixel United, the company distributes thousands of games through its bigfishgames.com storefront and mobile apps. It operates as a consumer-facing games company and does not currently publish a public developer API program, OpenAPI definition, or partner API surface; this profile tracks its public web presence for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bigger Games
providers.description: Bigger Games is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of index-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: entertainment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: BigScreen
providers.description: Bigscreen is a social virtual-reality company founded in 2014 by Darshan Shankar. Its flagship Bigscreen app lets people watch movies, mirror their Windows PC desktop, play games, and hang out with friends inside shared virtual rooms across major VR platforms. In 2023 the company shipped the Bigscreen Beyond, an ultra-compact, custom-fit OLED PC-VR headset, followed by the Beyond 2 line. Bigscreen is a consumer VR hardware and software company backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors; it does not currently operate a public developer program or REST API. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Blue Frog Gaming
providers.description: Blue Frog Gaming is a small independent game studio founded in 2007 by Matt Maroon and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2007 batch), based in Akron, Ohio. The company builds browser-based and social strategy games, best known for Starfleet Commander — a persistent, multi-universe game of resource management, alliance building, and fleet combat — along with Stardrift Empires (built with Syfy Games) and the sci-fi MMO ShadowRift. Blue Frog Gaming is a consumer game developer rather than an API-first platform: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API description. This record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it will be upgraded if and when a public API surface is discovered.

providers.name: Carbonated
providers.description: Carbonated Inc. is a mobile game developer founded in 2015 by industry veterans from Zynga, Electronic Arts, and Blizzard. The studio builds hardcore PvEvP (player-versus-environment-versus-player) games for phones and uses AI to help drive moment-to-moment gameplay. Its debut title is Mad World, currently in early-access sign-up. Carbonated also operates Carbyne, a proprietary live-ops platform that lets the team instantly modify almost every part of the game experience through a comprehensive set of web tools, built to support multiple games. Carbonated is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). As of this profile Carbonated publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this record captures the company identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CardMonster Inc.
providers.description: CardMonster turns ideas and brands into games. The company designs and publishes premium IP-based tabletop titles with global partners such as Disney and Krafton, and builds CardMonster Forge, an AI-powered tool that helps creators turn their own ideas into playable digital prototypes. From physical board games to an online playtesting platform, CardMonster connects creativity and technology to make game creation faster, smarter, and more accessible. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass CardMonster publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Chai Shots
providers.description: Chai Shots is a Hyderabad-based microdrama OTT streaming platform for vertical, short-form fiction where every episode runs under two minutes. Built by the Chai Bisket team (co-founders Sharath Chandra and Anurag Reddy), it is positioned as India's first regional short-series OTT, launching in Telugu and other regional Indian languages for Gen Z and tier II/III audiences. The platform offers pay-per-episode and unlimited subscription access, a creator-first "Clap" tipping feature, and an AI-native production workflow. It raised a $5M seed round co-led by InfoEdge Ventures and General Catalyst. Chai Shots is a consumer content app with no public developer/API surface at this time; this profile carries the company's identity and published web properties.

providers.name: Donnerwood Media
providers.description: Donnerwood Media was an early-stage social gaming and social entertainment company founded in 2005 by Sean Ryan and based in San Francisco. It operated Meez.com, an avatar-building platform that let consumers create customized 3D avatars usable across the web as personal identifiers, alongside a portfolio of social game properties. The company raised roughly $15.7M from Battery Ventures, transcosmos, and Allen & Company. It is now defunct — the Meez service went offline in December 2017 and its domain expired in March 2018 — so it exposes no live website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: Drivetime
providers.description: Drivetime (Drive.fm) was a voice-activated, hands-free in-car entertainment platform founded in 2018 by Niko Vuori, Justin Cooper, and Cory Johnson (veterans of Zynga and Rocket Games). The consumer mobile app delivered interactive trivia games, storytelling, quizzes, news, and audiobooks designed to be safe to play while driving, running on Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, and partnered with the Jeopardy game show for a channel narrated by Alex Trebek. The company raised roughly $15M across seed and later rounds, with backing from Canaan Partners, Makers Fund, the Amazon Alexa Fund, Google Assistant Investments, Sinai Ventures, Fuel Capital, and Access Ventures. Drivetime was a business-to-consumer product and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; as of this profiling the drive.fm / drivetime.fm domain and the associated App Store and Google Play listings no longer resolve, indicating the product has been discontinued.

providers.name: Encore Music Technologies
providers.description: Encore Music Technologies, Inc. ("Encore") is a consumer live-music technology company based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2020 by Ian Edelman, Jonathan Gray, and recording artist Kid Cudi. Its mobile app lets artists perform live inside custom augmented-reality environments directly from a phone while fans join, react, and pay artists in real time through gamified microtransactions such as a ten-cent "clap." The company raised a $9M seed round led by Battery Ventures in February 2022, with participation from 468 Capital, Kayak Ventures, Parade Ventures, and others. Encore ships consumer iOS and Android apps rather than a public developer platform; as of this pass it exposes no documented public API, and its marketing website (clapforencore.com) does not currently resolve to a live server.

providers.name: Endeavor
providers.description: Endeavor was a global sports and entertainment company representing talent and owning and operating events, with subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group. This repository tracks Endeavor as a corporate entity; no public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Endeavor Group Holdings
providers.description: Endeavor Group Holdings was a global sports and entertainment company that represented talent, owned and operated events, and provided licensing, marketing, and media services through subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent representation, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group, which now operates WME, 160over90, Pantheon Media Group, and IMG Licensing. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: EQL Games
providers.description: EQL Games is a Louisville, Kentucky based lottery-industry technology company that operates as an original game studio, third-party content aggregator, and boutique licensor for the global iLottery market. Its iLottery Marketplace aggregates a catalog of 300+ games from 24 partner studios behind a single integration point for lottery operators, while its EQL Labs innovation division builds original instant-win and eInstant titles that fold in licensed intellectual property and live sports. The company also represents brands across lottery verticals (instant scratch and eInstant) and reports serving 8 lottery clients. EQL Games was surfaced through Bullpen Capital's portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing and corporate web presence but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: ESPL
providers.description: ESPL (Esports Players League) is a Singapore-headquartered global esports tournament network and platform, founded in 2019, building an open, grassroots-focused ecosystem for amateur competitive gaming. It runs ESPL-branded online and on-ground tournaments across Asia, Europe, and the Americas with a mobile-first focus alongside PC and console titles, operated from its Singapore headquarters with regional offices in Cologne and Los Angeles. ESPL is a portfolio company of 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), which led its seed round in 2020. As of this enrichment pass ESPL publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface, and its espl.co domain did not resolve (DNS SERVFAIL) at probe time; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: EST
providers.description: EST (EST Media) is a Los Angeles-based media holding company founded by Jaeson Ma and Eric Tu that amplifies Asian stories and talent for global audiences. It operates three divisions: EST Studios, which develops, finances, produces, and sells Asian film and television projects; Eastern Standard Times, a Gen Z digital video platform sharing untold stories from Asia and its diaspora; and Established, a content studio partnering with global brands on advertising campaigns, influencer collaborations, commercials, and experiential events. EST Media is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile carries company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Fan Controlled Football
providers.description: Fan Controlled Football (FCF) was a professional indoor American football league in which fans voted on play calls in real time through a mobile app, playing a fast, 7-on-7 format staged at Pullman Yards in Atlanta and streamed to social and live-video audiences. The league drew high-profile athlete and celebrity team owners and investors and positioned itself as a fan-interactive, tech-driven sports and entertainment property. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. FCF paused operations and its public web presence (fcf.io) no longer serves a live site, so it currently exposes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface.

providers.name: Fifth Door
providers.description: Fifth Door is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) AI-native gaming startup founded by Amir Ghazvinian and Daniel Kan that lets anyone create, share, and play games simply by describing what they imagine, with no coding required. Its generative-AI platform turns natural-language prompts into playable, customizable games, aiming to collapse the time, cost, and technical complexity of traditional game development for players, creators, and studios. Backed by Felicis, the company runs a consumer web app and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: Flixster
providers.description: Flixster is an American movie-discovery and social entertainment brand founded in 2007 that let people rate and review movies, browse local showtimes, watch trailers, and share what they were watching. It grew into one of the largest movie communities on the web and mobile, and in 2011 was acquired by Warner Bros. together with Rotten Tomatoes; Fandango Media later acquired both Flixster and Rotten Tomatoes from Warner Bros. in 2016. The Flixster Video digital-locker service (built on UltraViolet) was shut down in 2019. The flixster.com property no longer operates as an independent consumer site — it now redirects to Fandango, and Flixster does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/brand record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Gamefam
providers.description: Gamefam is a gaming studio that builds and operates high-quality branded games and interactive experiences for Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences on platforms such as Roblox and Fortnite. It develops games, media campaigns, and amplification programs for 50+ brand partners (including LEGO, Adidas, Disney, and Netflix) and runs creator-facing programs such as Dev X and its Creator Fund. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Gamefam publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — its products are consumer game experiences distributed through third-party platforms.

providers.name: GetGlue
providers.description: GetGlue was a social-entertainment "check-in" network where users checked in to TV shows, movies, sports, music, and books to earn stickers and badges and see what friends were watching. Founded by Alex Iskold and backed by Union Square Ventures, it offered a public API and social graph for entertainment. GetGlue was acquired by i.TV in late 2013, rebranded to tvtag, and the service was discontinued. The getglue.com domain is now a parked lander with no live product, developer portal, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Happy Elements
providers.description: Happy Elements is a mobile game developer and publisher, backed by DCM Ventures, best known for free-to-play titles such as the Ensemble Stars! rhythm/idol franchise and Merc Storia. Operating across China and Japan, the company builds consumer entertainment games distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play rather than a public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector portfolio profile; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface, so the only machine-verifiable artifact is a probed domain-security posture for happyelements.com.

providers.name: Hidden Leaf Games
providers.description: Hidden Leaf Games is an independent video game development studio founded in 2019 and based in the United States. The studio builds competitive multiplayer games centered on competition, progression, and social play, with a stated mission of delivering a world-class experience where games are meant to be played together regardless of skill level or platform. The company is led by CEO David Li and President Bao Lam and raised seed funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2021. Hidden Leaf Games is a consumer gaming company and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile tracks it as a portfolio-sourced lead in the API Evangelist network for ongoing enrichment.

providers.name: Invisible Universe
providers.description: Invisible Universe is a consumer entertainment company building AI-powered animated intellectual property for social platforms — described by FastCompany as "building the Pixar of the internet one TikTok at a time." It has launched multiple animated franchises reaching millions of followers and billions of views across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube, and created Invisible Studio, a proprietary AI engine that compresses short-form animated content production from weeks to hours. Backed by Initialized Capital, it operates in the consumer/media sector. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Joyride
providers.description: Joyride was a mobile audio service that made driving more fun and more interesting, offering an in-car audio/entertainment experience for drivers and passengers. Founded by Jeff Chen (co-founder & CEO) and James Zhang (co-founder & CTO), the company raised a seed round from Cowboy Ventures and was subsequently acquired by Google, marking a successful exit. As a consumer mobile application it exposed no public developer API surface, and the product is no longer independently operated following the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Jubilee Inc
providers.description: Jubilee Inc (Jubilee Media) is a Los Angeles-based digital media production company that creates discussion-based and dating video shows designed to provoke thoughtful conversation and foster human connection across social and ideological divides. Its flagship YouTube programs include Middle Ground, Odd One Out, and Ranking, alongside sister dating channels such as Love Comma Nectar (Versus 1) and the reaction and behind-the-scenes brand TwoBilee. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API or developer platform at this time, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Kuwo Music
providers.description: Kuwo Music (酷我音乐) is a Chinese online music streaming service, founded in Beijing in 2005, that grew from a desktop music player into one of China's major consumer streaming apps across desktop, web, and mobile. Kuwo merged with Kugou under China Music Corporation, which was subsequently acquired by Tencent Music Entertainment Group, and Kuwo now operates as one of TME's music apps alongside QQ Music and Kugou. Kuwo entered the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead via Qiming. It is a consumer-facing streaming property rather than an API-first provider, and no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface has been verified for it.

providers.name: Lost Lake Games
providers.description: Lost Lake Games is a Seattle-based independent video game studio building narrative-driven games. The studio raised a $5.1M seed round in 2022 led by BITKRAFT Ventures with participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners, 1Up Ventures, and Moon Holdings, and describes itself as being at the beginning of its next big adventure. As a consumer game developer, Lost Lake does not currently operate a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; its web presence is a marketing site with an email signup and links to Steam, Discord, and Twitter/X. This profile captures the company's identity and public footprint within the API Evangelist network, surfaced originally as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: Magic Circle Studio
providers.description: Magic Circle Studio is a venture-backed consumer mobile game developer building social games designed to nourish relationships through cooperation, creativity, and playful shared experiences. Its flagship title, Magic Garden, launched on iOS in July 2025 and reached one million players in its first year, following the studio's earlier titles Truffle Hogs and a Magic Circle Discord activity that won Discord's Best Chill/Party Game award. The studio received pre-seed funding from General Catalyst in 2022 and joined the a16z Games SPEEDRUN accelerator in 2023. It is a direct-to-consumer game company with no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained as a network identity record.

providers.name: Meet Cute
providers.description: Meet Cute is a New York-based media company founded in 2019 by Naomi Shah that produces and distributes original scripted romantic-comedy audio programming, releasing bite-sized 15-minute rom-com stories as podcasts across platforms such as Apple Podcasts and Spotify. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Advancit Capital, and LocalGlobe, the company was acquired by Fox Entertainment in November 2025 to serve as a rapid-development content incubator for scripted and unscripted series. Meet Cute is a consumer media/content brand with no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile is retained as a company record.

providers.name: MoreTickets
providers.description: MoreTickets (摩天轮票务), operated by Shanghai Juqitech, is a next-generation internet performance ticketing marketplace founded in 2015. The platform lets consumers buy and sell tickets to concerts, stage plays, musicals, and sports events through a transparent, competitive pricing marketplace with standardized ticketing services. It operates primarily as a consumer-facing web and mobile marketplace and does not publish a public developer API or open platform. The company is backed by Qiming Venture Partners and has raised a reported $108M in funding.

providers.name: mSpot
providers.description: mSpot was a mobile cloud-based content service provider founded in 2004 by Daren Tsui (CEO) and Ed Ho (CTO) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company offered a cloud music locker that let users upload their music library and stream it from PCs, Macs, iPhone, iPad and Android devices, alongside a full-length movie rental service with content deals across Sony, Disney, Paramount, NBC/Universal, Lionsgate, Warner and others. mSpot raised roughly $2.3M in venture funding from Trinity Ventures and was acquired by Samsung Electronics in May 2012 (reported ~$8.8M) to power the Samsung Music Hub. The standalone mSpot product and brand were subsequently wound down and folded into Samsung; there is no active mSpot developer portal, API, or product surface today. This profile is retained as a historical network record.

providers.name: MySpace
providers.description: Myspace (Myspace LLC, part of the People / Entertainment Weekly Network) is a music and culture social platform focused on artist networking, music streaming, and editorial entertainment coverage. Originally one of the largest social networks of the 2000s, it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Myspace operates a consumer music/entertainment website only — its former developer platform (developer.myspace.com, OpenSocial-based) has been retired and no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or API documentation surface could be found. This profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only, with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Myxt
providers.description: Myxt is a consumer music streaming platform operated by Paper Phones Inc., built around the tagline "Musicians. Fans. Nothing in between." Instead of forced monthly subscriptions, Myxt uses an "unlock" model that lets artists monetize audio, session files, project files, images, and videos directly, while fans support creators without a recurring commitment and can chat with the artist after each unlock. Native iOS and Android apps extend access beyond the web. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network; during enrichment no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface was found.

providers.name: naturalmotion
providers.description: NaturalMotion is a mobile game developer founded in 2001 and now operating as part of Zynga under Take-Two Interactive, with games downloaded over six billion times across more than 175 countries. Known for titles such as CSR Racing, Star Wars Hunters, and the Euphoria and Morpheme animation technologies, the company builds and publishes consumer mobile games. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass NaturalMotion publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Neon Wild
providers.description: Neon Wild is a personalized children's entertainment platform backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) through its SPEEDRUN games program. Founded in New York by Troy Kirwin, it uses AI to transform a child's likeness into the hero of interactive digital books and narrative experiences distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface, and its former neonwild.com Squarespace site has expired. This profile remains a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: nWay
providers.description: nWay is a San Francisco-based multiplayer game developer and publisher founded in 2011, known for real-time synchronous PvP titles including Power Rangers: Legacy Wars (70M+ downloads), Power Rangers: Battle for the Grid, and the Web3 mech-combat game Wreck League. Its proprietary nWayPlay engine powers fast-paced cross-platform multiplayer across mobile, PC, and console. nWay was surfaced as a portfolio lead of cowboy-ventures. As a consumer gaming studio it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented API surface; enrichment probes of its website, /.well-known/security.txt, and /llms.txt returned no API artifacts.

providers.name: Parhelion Studio Co.
providers.description: Parhelion Studio Co. is an anime-focused game studio based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and a portfolio company of a16z (Speedrun Cohort 002). Founded by a team that met at the University of Michigan, the studio builds live-service anime mobile and PC games — including gacha titles and the tactical anime trading card game Echoes of Astra — publishing across Steam, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. Their mission is to make anime a global medium and to create long-lasting IP through games and technology. Parhelion Studio is a consumer entertainment company; a public, scan of its website (parhelion.gg), app-store listings, and the a16z Speedrun profile found no developer-facing API, SDK, MCP server, webhook, or other machine-readable API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead and enriched to confirm it has no public API program at this time.

providers.name: Partyphile
providers.description: Partyphile (formerly Guestlist.ph) is a Manila, Philippines nightlife and events startup that built a consumer mobile app for discovering clubs, bars, parties, and events, getting on club guest lists to waive cover charges and skip lines, and booking VIP tables. Founded by Ron Baetiong out of a University of Santo Tomas thesis, it raised seed funding from 500 Startups (500 Global) and Kickstart Ventures and planned Southeast Asia expansion. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company presents no public developer or API surface — its primary domain partyphile.com no longer resolves and partyphile.ph is unreachable — so no API artifacts exist to harvest; this remains a company identity profile.

providers.name: Peak Games
providers.description: Peak (Peak Games) is a global mobile game developer headquartered in Istanbul, Turkey, best known for the casual puzzle titles Toon Blast and Toy Blast, which reach roughly 40 million monthly active users worldwide. The studio was acquired by Zynga in 2020 and operates teams across game development, art, big data and data science, and cloud platform engineering. Peak publishes consumer mobile games and does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Penn National Gaming
providers.description: Penn National Gaming (now operating as Penn Entertainment) is one of the largest and most diversified regional gaming and racing companies in the United States, operating casinos and racetracks across multiple states. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: Piñata Farms
providers.description: Piñata Farms is a Los Angeles-based consumer entertainment company behind an AI video and meme-making mobile app that turns chats, photos, and trending templates into personalized memes and short AI-generated video messages. Backed by Index Ventures and Founders Fund, the product is delivered as an iOS/mobile consumer app served by a private backend at api.pinatafarm.com; the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead with a monitored (currently unavailable) marketing site and a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Platogo
providers.description: Platogo Interactive Entertainment GmbH is a Vienna, Austria based social casino gaming studio that builds and operates free-to-play slot and casino apps for mobile and web. Its flagship titles are Slotpark, a premium Vegas-style social slots app used by millions daily, and Gaminator, one of the largest social casino gaming communities on the web. The company localizes its games into more than 13 languages and works alongside industry partners including Greentube and Novomatic. Platogo is backed by Seedcamp. No public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Pocket Fm
providers.description: Pocket FM is an audio entertainment platform offering long-form audio series, audiobooks, and serialized stories across genres such as romance, fantasy, thriller, and horror. Listeners stream free episodes and unlock premium content through an in-app coins/store model, while writers and voice creators publish original work through the Pocket FM Studio. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass, Pocket FM operates as a consumer-facing mobile and web product and does not publish a public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Pop-Up Magazine
providers.description: Pop-Up Magazine is a live magazine created for a stage, a screen, and a live audience, produced by the team behind The California Sunday Magazine. Each production combines original nonfiction storytelling, live music, illustration, animation, and photography performed on tour in theaters across the United States. The company also operates Pop-Up Magazine Brand Studio, producing custom live and multimedia storytelling for brand partners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Pop-Up Magazine is a consumer media and live-events brand; it publishes a public promotional website but exposes no developer program, public API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface, so this profile is identity- and security-posture-only.

providers.name: Pose
providers.description: Pose (pose.vn) is a Vietnamese entertainment and lifestyle media publication based in Ho Chi Minh City, covering celebrity news, beauty pageants (including Miss Universe Vietnam), fashion, beauty, health, and film and television. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a company stub. As of this enrichment pass the site is a consumer-facing content publication monetized through advertising and sponsored content, with no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Radiant Entertainment
providers.description: Radiant Entertainment was an independent video game studio co-founded by brothers Tom and Tony Cannon, who also created the Evolution Championship Series (EVO), the premier fighting-game tournament. The studio was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and is known for the free-to-play fighting game Rising Thunder and the voxel city-building title Stonehearth. Radiant Entertainment was acquired by Riot Games in 2016 and its team was folded into Riot; the studio no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rascal Games
providers.description: Rascal Games is a game development studio founded by Rick and Jon, both experienced entrepreneurs previously at Blitz.gg and Discord. The studio is building "Project Wayward," a group-based PvE action-adventure game inspired by Sea of Thieves, Valheim, and Fortnite, with an emphasis on cooperative multiplayer experiences. Rascal Games raised a Series Seed round backed by a16z SPEEDRUN and industry veterans including Mitch Lasky. As a pre-launch game studio, Rascal Games publishes a marketing and careers site but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; the enrichment pass confirms there is currently no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Rec Room
providers.description: Rec Room is a cross-platform social gaming and user-generated-content platform where players hang out, play, and build their own rooms and games using in-app creation tools (Rec Room Studio and the visual Circuits scripting system). It runs on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Meta Quest VR, iOS, and Android with a shared avatar and economy. Founded in 2016 (originally as Against Gravity) and headquartered in Seattle, the company is backed by Index Ventures among other investors. Rec Room publishes a consumer platform at rec.net; no official public developer API or documented developer program was found during enrichment (the site is served behind Cloudflare and an internal api.rec.net host exists but is undocumented/unofficial).

providers.name: Scripps Networks Interactive
providers.description: Scripps Networks Interactive, Inc. (NASDAQ: SNI) was a Knoxville, Tennessee lifestyle media company that owned HGTV, Food Network, Travel Channel, DIY Network, Great American Country and Cooking Channel, plus digital properties including ulive. Discovery Communications completed its $14.6B acquisition on 2018-03-06 and renamed itself Discovery, Inc.; the brands now sit inside Warner Bros. Discovery. Scripps Networks Interactive no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer program, API or machine-readable contract. Its former corporate domain, scrippsnetworksinteractive.com, has since been re-registered by an unrelated party and now serves an Australian online-gambling affiliate site, so it must not be linked as a company property.

providers.name: Seed&Spark
providers.description: Seed&Spark is a crowdfunding and streaming platform for independent film and episodic content, combining a project crowdfunding marketplace for filmmakers with a subscription streaming service for independent films and series. Founded in 2012 and backed by Techstars, the company helps independent creators raise funds, build audiences, and distribute their work. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment (homepage and app paths sit behind Cloudflare bot protection; no api.* or developers.* subdomain resolves and no well-known API documents are published).

providers.name: Seriously
providers.description: Seriously Digital Entertainment is a mobile game studio best known for the Best Fiends match-3 puzzle franchise, a bug-versus-slug adventure set in the world of Minutia and available on iOS and Android. Founded in Helsinki with a Los Angeles presence and backed by Northzone, the studio was acquired by Playtika. It is a consumer entertainment company: its public web presence (seriously.com, which now redirects to bestfiends.com) is a game marketing and community site with app-store download links and social channels. Seriously publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Skypunk
providers.description: Skypunk is an independent game studio headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2021 to build new science-fiction multiplayer games. The studio is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and has raised approximately $750K in early funding. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Skypunk is a consumer game developer, not an API producer: its public presence is a studio marketing site and it publishes no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or any external API surface at this time.

providers.name: Small Giant Games
providers.description: Small Giant Games is a Helsinki, Finland based mobile game studio best known for the hit puzzle-RPG Empires & Puzzles. Founded in 2013, the studio was acquired by Zynga in 2018 (now part of Take-Two Interactive) and continues to operate its live free-to-play mobile titles. As a consumer mobile gaming company it publishes player-facing games and support resources rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and EQT Ventures and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline, which found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, package/SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface — only a live consumer marketing website.

providers.name: Sonantic
providers.description: Sonantic was a London-based AI voice company that built hyper-realistic, emotionally expressive text-to-speech models for entertainment, gaming, and film. The company is best known for recreating Val Kilmer's voice for Top Gun: Maverick after he lost his speaking voice to throat cancer. Spotify acquired Sonantic in June 2022 for a reported 93 million euros, and the underlying TTS technology has since been folded into Spotify products, most visibly the Spotify AI DJ feature launched in 2023. As of 2026, Sonantic no longer operates as a standalone product or public API. This apis.yml entry exists as a historical and archival record of the company, its technology, and its acquisition.

providers.name: Space Ape
providers.description: Space Ape Games is a London-based mobile game studio founded in 2012 and now part of Supercell, known for live-service mobile titles including Beatstar, Fastlane: Road to Revenge, Transformers: Earth Wars, Samurai Siege, and Rival Kingdoms. The studio operates in the consumer gaming sector and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; its primary web presence redirects to Supercell. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which found no public API surface and captured domain-security posture for the studio domain.

providers.name: Storia Originals, Inc.
providers.description: Storia Originals, Inc. (doing business as Storiaverse) was a Los Angeles-based consumer mobile entertainment startup founded in 2023 by Agnes Kozera and David Kierzkowski. Its Storiaverse app pioneered a patent-pending "read-watch" format blending short-form reading, animation, and audio, connecting writers and animators to publish and monetize original stories across sci-fi, fantasy, horror, mystery, and comedy, including adaptations of HarperCollins titles. It raised a pre-seed round led by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; both its marketing site (storia.io) and its iOS/Android app store listings are no longer reachable (all HTTP 404), indicating the product is inactive or has been wound down.

providers.name: Super
providers.description: Super (super.gs) is an early-stage consumer entertainment application built by Outpace Studios and backed by Bullpen Capital, positioned around the tagline "Entertainment you can cash out." As of mid-2026 the product is pre-launch: the public site is a single-page marketing and waitlist experience with no published developer platform, API, SDKs, or documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks Super as a portfolio lead and currently carries only a live domain-security probe of super.gs; it will be enriched further if and when the company ships a public API surface.

providers.name: Superplastic
providers.description: Superplastic is a designer-toy and entertainment brand that creates animated synthetic celebrities and collectible vinyl art toys, including the characters Janky, Guggimon, and Staffie, sold through its Shopify-powered online store. Based in Burlington, Vermont, the company blends animation, streetwear-style limited-edition drops, and collectible figures. It is a direct-to-consumer commerce and social-media brand and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its web and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Survios
providers.description: Survios is a virtual reality game studio that develops and publishes immersive VR titles across major platforms including PlayStation VR, Steam, Meta Quest, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch. Known for award-winning games such as Raw Data, Creed: Rise to Glory, The Walking Dead: Onslaught, Sprint Vector, Electronauts, and Alien: Rogue Incursion, the studio describes itself as one of the world's leading VR games studios. Backed by Lux Capital, Survios operates as a consumer games company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Syntertainment
providers.description: Syntertainment was an entertainment technology startup founded in 2012 in Berkeley, California by game designer Will Wright (creator of SimCity and The Sims), Avi Bar-Zeev, and Anya Wright, emerging from the Stupid Fun Club collective. The company set out to explore the intersection of entertainment and reality, blending real-world data and player experiences with game-like interactive media. It raised roughly $5M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Mayfield, SV Angel, and former Electronic Arts CEO John Riccitiello. The venture never shipped a public consumer product and is no longer active; its website (syntertainment.com) is offline and it exposes no public developer program, documentation, or API surface. This profile was surfaced from an a16z portfolio list and enriched to reflect the company's real, historical status.

providers.name: Tapastic
providers.description: Tapastic is the former brand of Tapas, a digital storytelling platform (Tapas Entertainment, a Kakao company) that hosts webcomics and web novels across romance, fantasy, action, drama, and other genres. Readers access serialized episodes through a free-with-premium model using an in-app "Ink" currency, and creators publish original and user-generated stories via the creators.tapas.io publishing portal. The original tapastic.com domain has been retired and now rebrands to tapas.io. As of this enrichment pass the platform exposes only a consumer web/mobile application and a content-creator publishing surface; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, developer portal, or documented webhook/event surface. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and remains a lead in the API Evangelist network with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Tastemade
providers.description: Tastemade is a modern media company producing food, travel, and home & design video programming for a global millennial and Gen-Z audience. Founded in 2012, it distributes short- and long-form video across social platforms, connected-TV apps, and its ad-supported and subscription Tastemade+ streaming service, and runs a branded-content studio for advertisers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of redpoint-ventures; enrichment found no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Tennis Channel
providers.description: Tennis Channel is a United States-based cable television network and direct-to-consumer streaming service dedicated to tennis and racquet sports, including live coverage and highlights from the ATP Tour, WTA Tour, Grand Slam events, and related pickleball and padel programming. Alongside its linear TV channel it operates a subscription streaming product (Tennis Channel / formerly Tennis Channel Plus) delivering live matches, on-demand video, news, rankings, and instructional content across web, mobile, and connected-TV apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Tennis Channel publishes a consumer streaming platform but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: The Icon League
providers.description: The Icon League is a five-a-side (small-sided) football entertainment league co-founded by former Real Madrid and Germany midfielder Toni Kroos and German streamer Elias Nerlich (Eliasn97), operated by The Icon League GmbH of Cologne, Germany (Amtsgericht Köln, HRB 117138). Played indoors in a US-style 14-team franchise format with two 12-minute halves and "Rulebreaker" mechanics designed to maximize attacking play, the league blends professional and amateur players and is distributed primarily through livestreams and social platforms to a young German-speaking audience. Season one generated more than 1.3 billion social-media impressions, and the league raised a €15M Series A (backed by HV Capital) to professionalize operations and expand across Europe. This is a consumer sports-and-media property; it publishes a public content website (teams, players, standings, matchdays, news, tickets, shop) but exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: thetab
providers.description: The Tab (thetab.com) is a UK-based digital media and entertainment publication operated by Digitalbox Publishing Ltd (Co Reg No. 09909897). It covers celebrity and reality-TV news, viral trends, gaming, politics, and university and campus culture across a network of youth-focused verticals, monetized primarily through advertising (advertise.thetab.com). Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, /.well-known/ discovery surface, or llms.txt (all probed and returned HTTP 404); this remains an editorial/advertising media property with no developer-facing product.

providers.name: Trendy Entertainment
providers.description: Trendy Entertainment was a Gainesville, Florida video game studio best known for the Dungeon Defenders tower-defense action-RPG franchise. Insight Venture Partners acquired the studio in 2012 for ~$18.2M and exited in 2019 when founder Augi Lye led an employee buyback and rebranded the company as Chromatic Games (chromatic.games). The only developer-facing surface the studio ever shipped is the Dungeon Defenders Development Kit — an Unreal Engine 3 game-mod SDK distributed as free Steam DLC — not a public web/HTTP API. Enrichment pass found no OpenAPI, REST API, developer portal, or client SDK registries: this is a games company with no programmable API surface, so most scored artifact types are N/A rather than missing.

providers.name: Trion Worlds
providers.description: Trion Worlds was an American video game developer and MMO publisher founded in 2006 in Redwood City, California by Lars Buttler and Jon Van Caneghem, and backed early by Trinity Ventures among others. It developed and operated massively multiplayer titles including Rift, Defiance, Trove and Atlas Reactor, published ArcheAge in Western markets, and ran the Glyph game-distribution client. The company was acquired by German publisher Gamigo in October 2018 and disbanded shortly after; its games, the Glyph platform and the trionworlds.com domain are now operated by Gamigo. Trion Worlds never published a public developer API or developer program, so this network profile carries company identity and domain-security signals only. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: Twenty-First Century Fox
providers.description: Twenty-First Century Fox was an American multinational mass media corporation that operated film, television, and cable assets before being largely acquired by The Walt Disney Company in 2019. Its remaining broadcasting and news assets continued under Fox Corporation. The company no longer exists as an independent entity and did not expose public developer APIs.

providers.name: Wave
providers.description: Wave is a virtual entertainment company that produces interactive, avatar-driven virtual concerts and immersive live music experiences known as "Waves." The platform streams stylized, real-time performances from major recording artists — including The Weeknd, Justin Bieber, John Legend, J Balvin, and Alison Wonderland — as animated avatars across VR headsets, desktop, mobile, and social video platforms, letting fans attend and interact with shows from anywhere. Wave is a consumer-facing entertainment and media product (accessed at wavexr.com) rather than a developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation. It was surfaced as a venture-portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, where this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: WeMash
providers.description: WeMash was a Los Angeles-based, cloud-based video mashup platform founded in 2014 that partnered with movie studios, news organizations, sports entities, and music labels to give creators legal access to premium content for derivative works, with monetization shared across rights holders. Backed by a roughly $420K seed round whose sole institutional investor was Andreessen Horowitz, the company is now defunct - wemash.com no longer resolves and no developer, documentation, or API surface remains to be catalogued.

providers.name: Wetpaint
providers.description: Wetpaint is a media brand operating wetpaint.com, an entertainment and lifestyle publication covering Hollywood gossip, celebrity news, TV series recaps and buzz, and pop-culture storytelling. Originally a Trinity Ventures-backed wiki/collaborative-media startup, the property today runs as an ad- and affiliate-supported editorial content site with no public developer program: as of this enrichment pass it exposes no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a media-sector company record.

providers.name: WiTag
providers.description: WiTag Inc is an augmented reality mobile gaming company founded in 2016 by Thomas Suarez that built AR laser tag gameplay using only a smartphone's built-in sensors and radios, with no extra hardware. Lightspeed Venture Partners led a seed investment in 2017. As of July 2026 the company appears dormant, its website witag.co no longer resolves in DNS, no app is listed in the Apple App Store, and no public API or developer surface was found.

providers.name: yplanapp
providers.description: YPlan (operated by Leanworks Limited) was a mobile-first event discovery and last-minute booking app founded in London in 2012 by Rytis Vitkauskas and Viktoras Jucikas. It offered a curated feed of things to do and same-day ticket booking across cities including London, Bristol, Dublin and New York, working with thousands of event partners. The company was acquired by Time Out Group plc in October 2016 and the consumer app was discontinued in 2017. The yplanapp.com domain now 301-redirects to checkout.timeout.com. No public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists; enrichment probing found no API artifacts, so this remains an identity-only record for a defunct company.

providers.name: Zingroll
providers.description: Zingroll is a consumer AI entertainment platform that generates personalized episodic video shows starring the user. A person uploads a single selfie and Zingroll casts them as the lead in an AI-generated series spanning up to 200 episodes across genres including action, romance, horror, and comedy, which can then be watched and shared. Backed by Accel, Zingroll operates in the AI media and generative-video space. The company runs a public consumer web application at zingroll.com but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile tracks it in the API Evangelist network as an AI-sector lead.

providers.name: National Football League
providers.description: The National Football League (NFL) is the premier professional American football league, comprised of 32 franchises divided between the AFC and NFC conferences. The NFL produces the Super Bowl and is the most-watched sports league in the United States. The league does not operate a public developer portal; statistical and play-by-play data feeds are licensed to partners (notably AWS, Amazon Web Services Next Gen Stats, Sportradar, and Genius Sports) and are not offered as a self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Warner Brothers
providers.description: A major American film and entertainment studio producing movies, television shows, and interactive entertainment. Part of Warner Bros. Discovery operating across theatrical, streaming, and gaming platforms.

providers.name: VeeFriends
providers.description: VeeFriends is a character-driven collectibles and entertainment company founded by Gary Vaynerchuk, built around 250+ original characters that embody human values like empathy, patience, and kindness. Operated by Vee Friends, LLC out of New York, the brand spans NFT collections (Series 1, Series 2, Iconics, Book Games), Topps Chrome trading cards and a trading card game, comic books and cartoons, collectible stickers and pins, apparel and plush merchandise, and the Burn Island platform where holders burn NFTs to unlock rare collectibles, events, and prizes. VeeFriends is an a16z portfolio company and publishes no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: Fantasy Akhada
providers.description: Fantasy Akhada is an Indian daily-fantasy-sports platform operated by Super Six Sports Gaming Private Limited (CIN U72900HR2019PTC083570) of Gurugram, Haryana, founded in 2020 by Amit Purohit, Sumit Kumar Jha, Sahil Ahuja, Amit Bhardwaj and Ankit Upreti, with cricket commentator Harsha Bhogle as brand ambassador. Users build virtual teams for real cricket, football, kabaddi, basketball and hockey fixtures and enter free and cash contests, with the platform taking a commission on entry fees; it marketed itself on the lowest commission rates in the category and claimed 3.5 to 4 million registered users. The product shipped only as a consumer iOS app and a sideloaded Android APK plus a React single-page web lobby - there is no developer program, public API, SDK, webhook surface or developer portal of any kind, and none has ever been published. As of the August 2026 probe the brand's own web presence is broken: www.fantasyakhada.com is a dangling CNAME to a deleted AWS ap-south-1 load balancer, the apex carries no address record, every backend service host referenced by the company's own JavaScript bundles has been withdrawn from DNS, and only stale static CloudFront/S3 builds remain. India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025 banned real-money online games nationwide in August 2025.

providers.name: National Basketball Association
providers.description: The National Basketball Association (NBA) is the premier men's professional basketball league in North America, comprised of 30 franchises (29 in the United States and 1 in Canada). The NBA does not operate a public developer portal; statistical, scoring, and play-by-play data feeds are licensed through official partners (notably Sportradar and Genius Sports). The stats.nba.com endpoints are not officially documented as a public API.

providers.name: Playtika Holding
providers.description: Playtika Holding is an Israel-based mobile gaming company and Fortune 1000 firm that develops and publishes free-to-play casual and casino-themed games such as Slotomania, Bingo Blitz, and Caesars Slots. The company operates a portfolio of social and casual mobile gaming titles distributed through major app stores and uses data-driven engagement and live operations to monetize its global player base. Playtika does not publish a public developer portal or external API.

providers.name: Talofa Games
providers.description: Talofa Games is a mobile game developer and publisher backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The studio builds social fitness games that turn real-world physical activity into cooperative multiplayer play. Its flagship title, Run Legends, is a free-to-play running RPG available on iOS and Android in which players' real-world runs and walks power team battles against monsters, and its newer title Monster Walk is in closed beta. Talofa Games is a consumer mobile-gaming company and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity and public web presence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Dreamscape Immersive
providers.description: Dreamscape Immersive is an entertainment and technology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Culver City, California, that produces story-based, full-roam virtual reality experiences in which up to six people share a physical stage and see fully rendered avatars of one another inside a virtual 3D environment. It operates location-based VR venues in the United States, licenses its platform to international operators, and is a partner in the Dreamscape Learn education joint venture. Its public surface is a consumer ticketing and booking website; as of August 2026 the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and the single backend its website calls is a private, key-gated AWS API Gateway host that returns 403 to anonymous requests.

Its portfolio spans Wallio, a collaborative finance app for couples and families; Blue Studios Education, an edutainment streaming and learning platform; Blue Studios Entertainment, a family-oriented media production division; and Blueniverse, the ecosystem tying the products together. providers.name: Qubit Smart Tickets
providers.description: Qubit Smart Tickets (Boletos Qubit) is a Colombian event-ticketing platform operating at boletosqubit.co, a Spanish-language consumer web application for buying and validating tickets to concerts, sports, and live events, with local payment methods including Nequi. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no publicly documented API, developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, SDKs, changelog, or /.well-known discovery endpoints; the only server-side surface reachable is an internal PHP backend not intended for public integration, so no API artifacts were generated.

providers.name: In-Fusio
providers.description: In-Fusio was a mobile entertainment company founded in 1998 in Bordeaux (Merignac), France, and one of the pioneers of the mobile games industry. In September 2000 it launched ExEn (Execution Engine), the first Java-based game engine dedicated entirely to mobile devices, competing with Sun Microsystems' J2ME, and partnered with Motorola on a client-side mobile gaming API for faster action and richer graphics. The company published games and community services across more than 70 wireless carriers and 140 handsets worldwide, with distribution deals including Verizon, Sprint, AT&T, Vodafone, Orange, Telefonica Moviles and China Mobile. It split its publishing and distribution divisions in January 2006, was acquired by Zenops in May 2007, entered administration in 2008, and went into compulsory liquidation in 2009. In-Fusio is recorded in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio company of Insight Partners; it operates no active developer platform or public API today.
